abstract: Nascent RNA production is a dynamic activity in eukaryotic cells that faithfully reflects the transcriptional activities of a cell population at a specific time point. To capture and quantify dynamic transcriptional activity at high temporal resolution, several methods have been developed, including global or precision run-on sequencing (GRO/PRO-seq) and transient transcriptome sequencing (TT-seq). TT-seq uses in-cell metabolic labeling of RNAs with 4-thiouridine (4sU) to specifically enrich newly synthesized, nascent RNAs. This strategy enables real-time measurement of transcriptional dynamics, including initiation, elongation, and termination, across the entire genome. It also enables the sensitive detection of various noncoding, nascent RNAs produced from regulatory elements, such as promoters and enhancers. By combining short pulse labeling with high-throughput sequencing, TT-seq can provide insights into RNA synthesis/decay rates, enhancer activity, and the kinetics of transcriptional regulation in response to various stimuli. The method has become a valuable tool for studying transcriptional control and gene regulation. Here, we describe the entire TT-seq workflow. Our protocol was based on the original TT-seq protocol, but we made several changes that streamlined the workflow.

abstract: Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) is a powerful reverse genetics tool that enables the transient knockdown of gene expression in plants by exploiting their natural antiviral defense mechanisms. This chapter presents a detailed protocol for applying a Cowpea severe mosaic virus (CPSMV)-based VIGS system to study gene function in soybean (Glycine max), with a focus on symbiotic root nodulation. VIGS allows systemic silencing of target genes, making it especially valuable to study pathways involving systemic signaling. The protocol includes Agrobacterium-mediated propagation of CPSMV variants in Nicotiana benthamiana, followed by mechanical inoculation of soybean plants and nodulation analysis. Detailed steps for vector construction, viral amplification, plant infection, and downstream molecular and phenotypic analyses are provided. This protocol is reproducible, accessible, and suitable for functional genomics studies in soybean, particularly for genes involved in nodulation but also in other developmental or stress-related processes.

abstract: Identification and characterization of essential Chlamydia-specific factors are vital for the generation of effective therapeutics and vaccines. Despite delays in the development of genetic tools for Chlamydia, significant advancements in Chlamydia genetic manipulation have been made over the last decade and a half, now allowing for the targeted interruption or deletion of chromosomal genes. However, because of the obligate intracellular nature of the bacteria and its unique biphasic developmental cycle, it remains challenging to inactivate essential genes and study the function of their encoded proteins. Here, we describe a method to generate conditional knockout Chlamydia mutants by introducing, prior to gene inactivation, a complementation plasmid containing the gene of interest under the control of an anhydrotetracycline (aTc)-inducible promoter. The chromosomal copy of the gene can then be selectively deleted to produce a conditional knockout mutant in which expression of the gene is controlled with aTc. We detail how this conditional knockout mutant can be used to determine if the targeted gene is essential for Chlamydia infection in cell culture and in vivo.

abstract: Understanding Chlamydia trachomatis infection requires physiologically relevant models tailored to various research questions. One of the main sites of C. trachomatis infection is the columnar epithelium of the endocervix; therefore, a model that accurately mimics the environment of endocervical epithelium is essential. Polarized cell models provide a valuable solution, offering a cost-effective yet biologically relevant alternative to conventional 2D culture systems and more complex and costly 3D or animal models. Immortalized human endocervical epithelial cells (A2EN cells) form a polarized monolayer on transwell membranes, reproducing key in vivo features, including tight junctions, mucus secretion, proinflammatory cytokine production, and hormone receptor expression, when maintained at low passage. This chapter outlines protocols for generating a polarized A2EN culture and assessing polarization through morphological, biochemical, and functional assays. Furthermore, we describe how C. trachomatis development can be monitored in polarized cells through microscopy, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, and reinfection assays.

abstract: Dictyostelia are aggregative multicellular (AGM) amoebae, whose life cycle alternates between solitary feeding and multicellular fruiting. This is by far the oldest and most diverse AGM lineage with an evolutionary depth equal to Vertebrata. The best-known species is the model organism, Dictyostelium discoideum. However, many traits studied in Dic. discoideum differ among the 170+ species, so a robust and comprehensive phylogeny is required to understand trait evolution. We constructed a dictyostelid-wide phylogeny with 173 deduced protein sequences using published data and 13 new proteomes. Phylogenetic analysis of the data with an Amoebozoan outgroup confidently places four poorly studied "orphan" taxa among its deepest branches. Thus, Synstelium polycarpum and Rostrostelium ellipticum appear as the deepest branches in Acytosteliaceae, supporting parallel evolution of the undifferentiated "acytostelid-like" morphology. Speleostelium caveatum, the only known cannibalistic species, is confirmed as the deepest branch in Raperosteliaceae, and Coremiostelium polycephalum is sister to both Dictyosteliaceae and Raperosteliaceae. The latter observation requires erecting a new family, which we designate Coremiosteliaceae. We also erect genus Porphyrostelium to accommodate the molecularly highly distinct and diverse collection of isolates previously grouped together as Dictyostelium purpureum.

abstract: Riboflavin is an essential vitamin widely used in pharmaceutical and feed applications, and its industrial production relies primarily on microbial fermentation. However, riboflavin biosynthesis in Escherichia coli is constrained by precursor availability and broader physiological regulation. In this study, a small regulatory RNA (sRNA)-mediated attenuation strategy was employed to systematically screen 91 genes across five functional modules. Twenty-three targets increased riboflavin production by more than 20%, and five key targets were further validated through genome-level modification. Combinatorial attenuation of rpe and yrfG, optimization of the nrfA-targeting sRNA expression cassette, and chromosomal reinforcement of the riboflavin operon were subsequently integrated to construct strain SN49M. Following fermentation medium optimization, SN49M produced 3153.3 mg/L riboflavin at 46 h in shake-flask cultivation with a yield of 193.4 mg/g glucose. In fed-batch fermentation, SN49M reached 20.5 g/L riboflavin within 72 h, with an overall yield of 178.9 mg/g glucose, representing the highest reported glucose-based riboflavin yield achieved by microbial fermentation. This work establishes a systematic and tunable framework for discovering and integrating metabolic and physiological perturbations, providing an effective strategy for improving carbon efficiency in microbial riboflavin production.

abstract: Epigenetic regulation provides a dynamic and reversible layer of gene control that functions independently of changes in DNA sequence, primarily mediated by DNA methylation, histone modifications, and higher-order chromatin organization. Aberrant epigenetic states contribute to a wide range of human diseases. However, conventional epigenetic therapies based on small-molecule inhibitors lack locus specificity and often cause global chromatin disturbances. The emergence of programmable epigenetic editing technologies has transformed the field by enabling targeted rewriting of chromatin states at defined genomic loci. Catalytically inactive CRISPR/Cas9 platforms fused to transcriptional activators, repressors, or chromatin-modifying enzymes now allow precise addition or removal of epigenetic marks without altering the underlying DNA sequence. This chapter provides an overview of the conceptual and technical foundations of CRISPR-based epigenetic editing, including tools for gene activation and repression, DNA methylation, histone modifications, and multiplexed systems that permit coordinated regulation of multiple genomic loci or epigenetic marks. Delivery methods for in vitro and in vivo applications are discussed, with an emphasis on viral and nonviral platforms that enable tissue-specific, durable gene regulation. Finally, recent preclinical and clinical studies highlight the potential of programmable epigenetic editing as a next-generation therapy for precise and reversible gene control.

abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is not only a high-resolution imaging technique but also a sensitive tool able to study biomechanical properties of biosamples (biomolecules, cells) in native conditions-i.e., in buffered solutions (culturing media) and stable temperature (mostly 37°C). Micromechanical transducers (cantilevers) are often used to map surface stiffness geometry, elastic, and contact parameters of living cells; however, they can also be used to monitor time course of dynamic forces (beating), their rate, and other biomechanical properties of cardiomyocyte contractility. Here we describe the construction of an AFM-based biosensor setup designed to study the biomechanical properties of cardiomyocyte clusters, using standard uncoated silicon nitride cantilevers. Force-time curves (mechanocardiograms, MCG) are recorded natively and in the presence of cardiomyocyte-contraction-affecting drugs (e.g., isoproterenol, metoprolol) in the medium, under physiological conditions. The average value of contraction force and the beat rate as basic biomechanical parameters represent pharmacological indicators of different phenotype features. Robustness, low computational requirements, and optimal spatial sensitivity (detection limit 200 pN or 20 nm) are the main advantages of the presented method.

abstract: Genome editing based on engineered CRISPR systems is advancing rapidly, with the field increasingly moving toward approaches that avoid the induction of mutagenic double-stranded DNA breaks (e.g., RNA-programmable base editing, prime editing, and donor DNA transposition). These nuclease-free strategies often rely on large or multi-component molecular assemblies that can include gene-sized donor DNA substrates. There is, nonetheless, a paucity of vehicles capable of delivering such large and complex genome-editing components effectively and, ideally, in defined stoichiometric ratios. High-capacity adenoviral vector particles (AdVPs) offer an attractive set of features to address these challenges, including robust cell transduction levels regardless of mitotic status, exceptional payload capacity (up to ~36 kb), strict chromosomal nonintegrating character, and the complete absence of viral coding sequences. Hence, AdVPs can serve as biological nanoparticles suitable for the evaluation and application of next-generation CRISPR technologies in physiologically relevant cellular contexts, regardless of the size and number of the attendant tools. Here, after summarizing the key characteristics of earlier- and latest-generation adenoviral vector platforms, we describe protocols for producing AdVPs, including vectors that deliver multiplexing, prime-editing, and orthogonal nuclease constructs. Finally, we highlight important considerations for designing AdVP production reagents and validate a storage buffer that preserves AdVP functionality after repeated freeze-thaw cycles.

abstract: Conventional treatments often face challenges such as the limited ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier (BBB). The Doxorubicin-loaded graphene oxide/magnetite (DOX/GO/Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>) nanocomplex offers a promising platform due to GO's high surface area and pH-sensitive release, and Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>'s magnetic properties. This protocol describes the methodology for evaluating the cytotoxicity of free DOX versus the DOX/GO/Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> nanocomplex in the A-172 glioblastoma cell line, followed by advanced bioinformatics analysis to identify gene networks and indirect pathways that enhance the nanomaterial's biocompatibility. The methodology integrates the MTT assay, real-time PCR for apoptosis genes (Casp3, Bax, and Bcl-2), and advanced analysis, including protein-protein interaction (PPI) networking, clustering, and promoter motif analysis. The analysis indicated that miR-92a-2-5p is a potential therapeutic target for preventing myocardial damage and enhancing biocompatibility. The findings highlight key regulatory pathways that indirectly boost nanodrug biocompatibility through the modulation of secondary components like miRNAs and cellular stress mechanisms.

abstract: Root hairs play pivotal roles in nutrient and water acquisition and in plant-microbe interactions. Consequently, understanding the mechanisms underlying root hair development and their regulatory pathways is an important aspect of plant physiology research. Quantifying root hairs and root hair length is often essential in such studies, but is labor-intensive and prone to subjectivity. The availability of straightforward tools for automated root hair measurements is limited, and existing options are often tailored for specific images or do not measure individual root hairs. To address this, we developed RootHairML, a flexible and simple Python-based machine learning tool designed for efficient quantification of root hair lengths. Based on labeled images and pixel features, RootHairML trains a Random Forest model to enable the detection of root hairs in new images. It provides measurements of individual root hair lengths per image and generates annotated images showing all detected root hairs, allowing for manual verification and adjustments. Here, we describe and showcase the use of RootHairML. Overall, RootHairML offers a valuable tool for root hair analysis, enabling researchers to increase data collection and enhance the reproducibility of root hair studies.

abstract: Cardiac organoids are increasingly used to model human cardiac development and disease, but their small size often limits molecular characterization, especially if different approaches and protocols are necessary to extract and quantify metabolites and lipids. Here, we present a multistep workflow for combined targeted free amino-acid (FAA) based metabolomic and lipidomic profiling from a single pooled cardiac organoid sample. The protocol covers organoid harvesting, detergent-assisted lysis, and a modified Folch extraction that generates an organic phase for lipid analysis and an aqueous phase for FAA metabolite analysis. Lipids are quantified by Liquid Chromatography Electrospray Ionization Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-ESI-MS/MS) in Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM) mode using class-matched external standards and an internal standard to support calibration and reduce technical variability. Free amino acids and derivatives are analyzed from the same sample after filtration, drying, and AccQ-Tag derivatization, with norvaline as an internal standard. Together, this approach maximizes information yield from limited material and enables integrated analysis of metabolic and lipid pathways within the same biological specimen, facilitating organoid-based studies of cardiac maturation, disease modeling, and pharmacological responses.

abstract: Mungbean (Vigna radiata L.) is a major pulse crop cultivated extensively across Asia and is considered an important model species among legumes because of its diploid genome and relatively small genome size. The availability of reliable, economical, and highly polymorphic molecular markers is critical for assessing genetic diversity, constructing linkage maps, and implementing functional genomics-based breeding programs. Among the available marker systems, simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers are highly polymorphic, abundant, co-dominant, and extensively used for allelic characterization across diverse crop species. This chapter describes the methodology for developing SSR markers and their use in genetic diversity studies in mungbean. Genome-wide SSR screening is performed to identify SSR motifs in the mungbean whole-genome sequence using the Phobos tandem repeat detection tool. The identified SSR motifs are annotated and categorized based on motif length, repeat type, and chromosomal location to facilitate the selection of informative loci for marker development. Primers are designed for selected SSR loci using appropriate flanking sequences and subsequently validated through PCR amplification across a panel of diverse mungbean genotypes. The polymorphism of these SSR markers is assessed by analyzing distinct and reproducible amplification patterns. The developed SSR markers constitute a valuable genomic resource for genetic diversity studies, molecular characterization, and genomics-assisted breeding applications in mungbean.

abstract: Two key factors required for pre-mRNA 3' end processing, CPSF73 and PCF11, are linked to poor cancer prognosis, yet their oncogenic roles remain unclear due to their dual function in transcription termination. Using a colorectal cancer (CRC) progression model, we show that primary tumor cells depend on high CPSF73 and PCF11 levels, whereas metastatic cells are less sensitive. This dependency is not explained by alternative polyadenylation (APA) or transcription-replication conflicts. Instead, we identify an uncoupling of 3' cleavage and transcription termination during CRC progression. Primary tumor cells exhibit a global shift toward proximal termination alongside distal APA usage, while metastatic cells partially revert to normal termination patterns and favor proximal APA. Notably, the distance between 3' cleavage and termination is nearly halved in primary tumor cells compared with normal cells and becomes particularly short in oncogenes. Reduced cleavage-termination distance correlates with increased gene expression both within and across cell states. These findings identify a previously unrecognized link between transcription termination architecture and gene expression regulation.

abstract: Lignin accounts for up to one-third of plant biomass, making it the second most abundant biopolymer on Earth. The thermophilic ascomycete Myceliophthora thermophila is a well-established platform to produce chemicals from plant biomass. However, its capacity for lignin metabolism remains largely unexplored. This study demonstrates that M. thermophila can remodel lignin and metabolize a broad spectrum of lignin-derived aromatic monomers. By integrating transcriptomic profiling with targeted gene deletions, we mapped the key metabolic pathways for these aromatic compounds. Specifically, we found that M. thermophila funnels diverse p-hydroxyphenyl (H) and guaiacyl (G) aromatic monomers into the 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid (protocatechuic acid, 3,4-DHB) branch of the β-ketoadipate pathway. Disrupting the protocatechuate hydroxylase and 3,4-dioxygenase genes successfully redirected metabolic flux, achieving 42.5‒95.8% molar yields of 3,4-DHB from H- and G-type monomers. Notably, the engineered strains achieved direct 3,4-DHB production from raw corncob. These findings provide new insights into the metabolism of lignin-derived aromatic compounds in M. thermophila and establish a foundation for integrated lignocellulose biorefineries and aromatic bioprocessing.

abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m<sup>6</sup>A) is a prevalent endogenous modification in mammalian mRNAs as well as chromatin-associated RNAs (caRNAs). Recently developed GLORI-seq, which chemically converts unmodified adenosine to inosine, enables absolute quantification of single-base-resolution m<sup>6</sup>A sites on mRNAs. However, since GLORI-seq generates short-transited reads with mainly three kinds of nucleotides, applying it to caRNAs with a large fraction of intronic and intergenic regions poses additional challenges. In our recent study, we simply optimized the library construction of GLORI-seq to enrich long cDNA fragments for subsequent sequencing, resulting in significantly promoted read length and mapping accuracy of GLORI-seq on caRNAs. Here, we describe the detailed protocol of optimized GLORI-seq of caRNAs to facilitate studies on m<sup>6</sup>A in caRNAs.

abstract: The efficacy of single-modal chemodynamic therapy (CDT) is often restricted by the antioxidant scavenging of overexpressed glutathione (GSH) within the tumor microenvironment (TME) and insufficient catalytic kinetics. Meanwhile, traditional photothermal therapy (PTT) also faces bottlenecks of a single therapeutic mechanism and low photothermal conversion efficiency, leading to unsatisfactory overall anti-tumor outcomes. To address these challenges, we constructed a smart-responsive, core-shell multifunctional nanotheranostic platform for near-infrared-II (NIR-II) photoacoustic (PA) imaging-guided synergistic PTT/CDT. This platform utilizes copper sulfide nanoparticles (CuS) as the photothermal core, conformally coated in situ with an Fe-tannic acid (TF) metal-phenolic network (MPN) shell (CuS@TF). In the mildly acidic TME, the TF shell dissociates to expose Fe/Cu bimetallic catalytic centers possessing excellent intrinsic peroxidase-like and catalase-like activities. Driven by the synergistic reduction of endogenous GSH and tannic acid, CuS@TF not only effectively depletes antioxidant GSH but also efficiently modulates H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> metabolism, triggering a cascade burst of highly toxic hydroxyl radicals (·OH). Furthermore, under 1064 nm laser irradiation, the highly efficient localized hyperthermia generated by the CuS core not only directly ablates the tumor but also thermodynamically boosts the catalytic kinetics of the nanozymes, achieving profound PTT-sensitized CDT. Systematic in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate that, under the precise navigation of PA imaging, CuS@TF exhibits remarkable tumor eradication efficacy (with a tumor inhibition rate of ~ 96.2%) and excellent in vivo biosafety. This work provides a novel design paradigm for the development of precise synergistic tumor theranostics based on multifunctional nanozymes.

abstract: In the Metaphysical Foundations of Natural Science, Kant famously argues that chemistry is not a proper science because chemistry does not allow for the application of mathematics. Although existing work on Kant and chemistry has greatly clarified many aspects of Kant's views on chemistry, a contextualized account of Kant's views on chemistry in relation to the chemistry books of his day is still a desideratum of Kant scholarship. In this article, I relate Kant's views on chemistry to the views of Stahl (1659-1734), Wiegleb (1732-1800), Erxleben (1744-1777), Weigel (1748-1831), Lavoisier (1743-1794), and Gren (1760-1798). I will highlight the structure and method of chemistry in Kant's time, arguing that chemistry was construed as ideally an axiomatic science in which non-fundamental judgments are deductively derived from fundamental judgments. Kant's denial that chemistry is a proper science can be fruitfully understood as a denial that chemistry has attained a proper axiomatic form. In line with this interpretation, I argue that it is not the case, as McNulty claims, that for Kant there are chemical laws.

abstract: In the academic year 2024/25, the EuChemS Division on Chemistry and the Environment (DCE) conducted a Europe-wide survey of higher education programmes that include Environmental Chemistry, either as the principal discipline or as embedded content in interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary curricula. Information on 300 programmes was collected from universities in 31 countries, i.e. 113 at the 1st, 156 at the 2nd and 31 at the 3rd study level. Respectively, 42%, 35% and 19% of the programmes shared details on the contents, teaching tools used, needs and future plans, while the rest of the responding programmes shared only basic information. With basic information on additional 159 1st and 2nd study level programmes based on web search by the authors (mostly for non-responsive countries), in total, 428 programmes at the 1st and the 2nd study level were identified. Since response rate varied dramatically across countries, the representativeness was severely undermined the findings for Europe as a whole. From the information collected from programmes which responded, it was found that multidisciplinary and/or environmental compartment-related approaches are present in programmes' design early, even from 1st level of education and more diverse at the 2nd level. Environmental Chemistry is taught in science programmes containing the terms 'environment(-al)', 'Chemistry', 'Geoscience' and 'Toxicology', but also quite frequently in engineering programmes. The water, climate, protection and sustainability themes are very common. A wide variety of programmes clearly reflects the importance of knowledge about the behaviour and effects of chemicals (including accompanying substances and waste products) in the environment for the training of experts in a variety of professions and occupational fields. The analysis of the contents of programmes with Environmental Chemistry as their principal discipline suggests that there is no uniform understanding of what exactly constitutes the discipline as a main or important topic within an interdisciplinary curriculum, most probably as a consequence of very broad discipline's boundaries. Greater consistency and better comparability of the content, skills and qualifications offered by degree programmes to be acquired therein could be achieved through a coordinated effort which would better define core contents.

abstract: Strongly overlapping voltammetric signals limit the individual determination of capsaicin (CAP) and dihydrocapsaicin (DHC) in pepper extracts. This study evaluated square-wave voltammetry (SWV) combined with Lorentzian signal deconvolution using HPLC as a reference method. Eleven commercially available Carolina Reaper-derived colour morphs were represented by one pooled sample each. Reliable deconvolution was achieved for nine samples, with the resulting individual CAP and DHC contents showing good agreement with HPLC measurements. Separately, total CAP and DHC contents determined by SWV and HPLC were strongly correlated (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.992). Among the analysed samples representing different colour morphs, Stinger and Rustic had the highest combined CAP and DHC contents, whereas Cream, Olive, Mustard, and Yellow had lower levels. These findings support the feasibility of the deconvolution approach for the successfully resolved extracts and provide an exploratory chemical comparison of the sampled commercial morphs.

abstract: We present a simple, practical workflow for annotating tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data of small molecules using advanced machine learning and a reference library. The discovery and structural characterization of small molecules is central to biology, chemistry, and medicine. MS/MS has become the leading technology for this task, yet the majority of spectra from untargeted metabolomics remain unannotated, limiting our understanding of the underlying chemical diversity. Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping many areas of science, and mass spectrometry is no exception. In this chapter, we introduce a practical workflow for annotating MS/MS data using two complementary resources: DreaMS, a foundation model for mass spectrometry, and MassSpecGym, a large reference library and benchmarking platform. DreaMS embeds mass spectra into a representation space where structural similarity is preserved, and MassSpecGym provides anchor points for retrieving identical or related molecules. Together, they form an ecosystem that enables efficient annotation of experimental MS/MS data. We demonstrate this approach on alkaloid data from Piper fimbriulatum, showing how DreaMS can retrieve exact matches or place unannotated spectra alongside structurally related compounds. All steps are provided as easy-to-follow protocols, designed to run on standard hardware and requiring no modifications to existing metabolomics pipelines. Readers will learn how to integrate AI tools into their own workflows for compound annotation, molecular networking, and discovery. Overall, this chapter aims to empower biologists and chemists to harness machine learning for metabolomics, transforming unannotated spectra into interpretable chemical knowledge.

abstract: Coumarins, as widely used organic small molecules, have been extensively exploited for the construction of fluorescent probes. However, there are relatively few reports on their multifunctional applications and the related researches on the structure-activity relationship. In this work, two 3-cyanocoumarin compounds named as MC and MBC with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics were designed and synthesized. Due to its excellent optical properties, MBC has been developed as a fluorescent anti-counterfeiting ink. In addition, MBC can also be used as a fluorescent probe for detecting some typical nitroaromatic compounds (NACs), such as picric acid (PA) and 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP), with limits of detection as low as 3.79 × 10<sup>-8</sup> and 6.20 × 10<sup>-8</sup> M, respectively. At the same time, two D-π-A type near-infrared fluorescent molecules named as MC-TPA and MBC-TPA were designed and synthesized by using two 3-cyanocoumarins (MC and MBC) as electron acceptors and 4-formyl triphenylamine (TPA) as an electron donor, respectively. Both MC-TPA and MBC-TPA molecules can exhibit AIE characteristics and obvious mechanofluorochromic (MFC) behavior. Due to the excellent color contrast, MC-TPA has been employed for inkless writing. Notably, it can be reused after being erased with dichloromethane (DCM) vapor. Based on single-crystal analysis and theoretical calculations, the structure-activity relationship accounting for diverse functional performances was explored. This serial work provides a solid foundation for the design, synthesis, and application of novel multifunctional fluorescent molecules.

abstract: This study presents haemoglobin functionalised chitosan-coated magnetic nanoparticles (Fe₃O₄-Cs-Hb) engineered as advanced carriers for chlorin e6 (Ce6) in photodynamic therapy (PDT). Chitosan shells were modified with long-distance amino groups and used to immobilise haemoglobin via amino- or carboxyl-directed conjugation, yielding systems with distinct physicochemical profiles. Hb immobilisation substantially increased Ce6 loading depending on the conjugation route. Drug release kinetics also shifted markedly: Hb-modified systems reduced the initial burst effect by 20-35% and prolonged release over 24 h. ROS-generation studies showed that Hb conjugation enhanced singlet oxygen production by 40-70% relative to non-modified carriers, with Fe₃O₄-Cs-3-Hb(a) providing the highest ROS yield for physically adsorbed Ce6, while Fe₃O₄-Cs-3-Hb(c) maximised ROS output for chemically bound Ce6. These two formulations also displayed the strongest photodynamic activity in HeLa cells, reducing EC₅₀ values from ~0,25-0,35 mg/mL (Hb-free systems) to 0,09-0,12 mg/mL (physically bound Ce6) and to 0,05-0,10 mg/mL (chemically bound Ce6). Collectively, the results demonstrate that haemoglobin imparts synergistic benefits, improving Ce6 loading, stabilising release, and significantly increasing PDT efficiency, highlighting its value as a functional component for next-generation phototherapeutic nanocarriers.

abstract: Diabetes mellitus remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of new therapeutic agents targeting key enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism. In this study, ten novel imidazo-thiazole-thiazolidinone hybrids were designed, synthesized and their structural integrity was confirmed through <sup>1</sup>H NMR and <sup>13</sup>C NMR along with mass determination by HREI-MS. After characterization, each derivative was subjected to in-vitro evaluation using acarbose (reference) to assess their anti-diabetic potential through the inhibition of key enzymes. Compound 3 and 6 with IC<sub>50</sub> values 3.20 ± 0.20 μM, 2.10 ± 0.30 μM for α-amylase and 3.70 ± 0.30 μM, 2.60 ± 0.20 μM for α-glucosidase acted as the excellent inhibitors, markedly affecting rate of enzymatic reactions, with kinetic studies revealing their mode of inhibition. The SAR analysis revealed key substituents enhanced ligand-enzyme affinity, supported by molecular docking showing their specific binding. Furthermore, in-vivo cytotoxic assessment in rat models was performed to examine toxicological aspects and biocompatibility of synthesized compounds. Pharmacophore modeling, DFT calculations and MD simulations were also conducted to provide mechanistic insights. Comprehensive ADMET analysis including bioavailability, toxicity prediction, oral suitability and drug-likeness together with in-vivo safety evaluation complemented the in-vitro and computational findings, demonstrating these imidazo-thiazole based thiazolidinone derivatives hold promise as effective therapeutics against diabetes mellitus.

abstract: The synthesis routes, crystal and molecular structures, and controlled thermal decomposition reactions of two [pentamminecobalt(iii) compounds having a coordinated chromate ion, [Co(NH3)5CrO4]Cl (compound 1) and [Co(NH3)5CrO4]2CrO4 (compound 2) were studied experimentally. Quantum chemical optimizations and QTAIM calculations were performed for compounds 1 and 2, and the selected Bond Critical Points (BCPs) properties were discussed. The extended hydrogen-bond network between the coordinated chromate ions and ammonia ligands acts as reactive redox reaction centres, and both compounds show solid-phase quasi-intramolecular redox reactions with the formation of Co[Co0.5Cr1.5O3.75] and Co[Co0.2Cr1.8O3.90] nanosized regular spinels with nominal Co : Cr = 1 : 1 and 2 : 3 molar ratios, respectively. The tetrahedral positions of these spinels are filled with CoII ions. The octahedral positions of 2 : 3 and 1 : 1 spinels prepared in air are filled CrIII and mainly with CoIII ions. The 2 : 3 spinel prepared under N2 shows a similar distribution of ions, whereas the 1 : 1 spinel prepared under N2 contains only CoII ions at T-4, and CrIII, CoIII, and CoII ions at the OC-6 positions, resulting in a strongly defective structure. The position of the chromate ions (inner-sphere coordinated or outer-sphere non-coordinated) plays an important role in the quasi-intramolecular redox reactions and thermal decomposition characteristics of compounds 1 and 2. The inner-sphere coordinated chromate ions of both compounds took part in redox reactions with their own coordinated ammonia only after the loss of the fifth ammonia, in an endothermic ligand-releasing and an exothermic redox reaction mediated by the outer-sphere chromate ion for compounds 1 and 2, respectively. The cobalt(iii) content of both complexes is also reduced completely to cobalt(ii). These spinels were proven to be active catalysts in the visible-light-driven photocatalytic oxidation of rhodamine B with H2O2.

abstract: Chemodynamic therapy (CDT) generates cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals (•OH) in tumors via Fenton/Fenton-like reactions using elevated H₂O₂ and acidity. However, its clinical potential is limited by poor tumor selectivity and the difficulty in balancing catalytic metal ion doses with toxicity. In this work, using HPBio (2-Pyridinecarboxaldehyde biotin bis-hydrazide) as the ligand, a biotinylated tri-nuclear copper(II) complex of POBio-Cu<sub>3</sub> has been in-situ synthesized. The solution assemble behavior and in-situ oxidation process has been investigated by time-dependent ESI-MS technology. In the atomically precise POBio-Cu<sub>3</sub>, biotin moiety was acting as a cancer-targeting unit and multi-nuclear Cu(II) core as a GSH depletor for augmented CDT effect. POBio-Cu<sub>3</sub> could preferentially accumulate in cancerous Hep-G2 cells, due to the cell discrepancy toward normal WI38 cells. The Cu(II) centers in POBio-Cu<sub>3</sub> were available for consuming glutathione (GSH) and amplifying oxidative stress. Furthermore, the results of in vivo experiments showed that POBio-Cu<sub>3</sub> could remarkably inhibit tumor growth without significant damage to major organs.

abstract: Cyclodextrin-based metal-organic frameworks (CD-MOFs) combine molecular host cavities with framework-generated porosity, but their rational use in drug delivery requires clearer links between guest localization, host-guest interactions, and release. This critical narrative review integrates experimental and computational evidence for native α-, β-, and γ-CD-MOFs, distinguishing them from modified, composite, and MOF-derived carriers. A claim-specific evidence hierarchy separates spatially resolved observations, indirect experimental support, and computational inference. Guest localization depends on molecular dimensions, ionization, polarity, aperture accessibility, loading level, and processing history. Different loadings can favor distinct occupancy patterns, surface association, or guest-rich domains; these comparative states do not establish dynamic redistribution without time-resolved evidence. Stabilization generally involves cooperative hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic and dispersion interactions, and electrostatic or cation-associated contributions. Release may reflect framework transformation or dissolution, diffusion through persistent or added barriers, host-guest dissociation, and subsequent complexation, aggregation, or recrystallization. Similar release profiles can therefore arise from different mechanisms. A diagnostic framework links release interpretation to carrier persistence, guest speciation, medium chemistry, and analytical sampling, while source-specific loading definitions constrain quantitative comparisons. Molecular simulations provide candidate configurations and pathways but require experimental validation; kinetic fits alone do not identify microscopic release mechanisms. This synthesis establishes a structure-occupancy-transport framework and identifies the paired structural, time-resolved, and solution-state measurements needed for more predictable CD-MOF-based drug delivery.

abstract: Two approaches for the enzymatic synthesis of DNA oligonucleotides (ONs) bearing multiple site-specific modifications were explored. The first approach based on repeated single nucleotide extension (SNI) and reverse transcription from RNA template with Bst 3.0 DNA polymerase followed by digestion and exchange of template efficiently produced an ON with single modification, but the second round gave mixtures of full-length and truncated products. The second approach was based on repeated cycles of SNI and primer extension from a DNA template followed by λ exonuclease digestion and exchange of the template and it worked very well even for consecutive incorporation of three different base-modified nucleotides at specific positions. This was demonstrated on the synthesis of a molecular beacon bearing Cy3 and Cy5 fluorophores for the FRET detection of target RNA. The method is an efficient single-tube operation that does not require separation and purification of intermediates and gives clean ONs labeled at desired positions.

abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), branched SCFAs, and their precursors (lactic, succinic, pyruvic acids) are key microbial metabolites relevant to gut function and are present in fermented foods. This study reports the transfer, development, and validation of a rapid capillary electrophoresis method with diode-array detection (indirect UV) for the simultaneous determination of 12 biologically important organic acids in <15 min. Starting from a commercial methodology, background electrolyte composition and separation voltage were optimised. The method was validated according to ICH Q2(R2). Linearity was confirmed from LOQ to 100 μg/mL, with LOQs of 1.53-5.76 μg/mL. Precision and trueness were satisfactory (CV ≤ 7.6%, |RE| ≤ 7.5%), matrix effects ranged from 80 to 121%, and selectivity was adequate. Applicability was demonstrated by analysing 11 fermented vegetable juices. Finally, the RGBfast model benchmarking against literature methods supported the method's suitability for routine profiling of organic acids in fermented foods.

abstract: Norfloxacin (NFC) residues in food products remain a concern because of their potential contribution to antimicrobial resistance and adverse health effects. This study presents a disposable electrochemical method for the selective determination of NFC based on template-derived molecular recognition cavities integrated with a conductive AgNWs/MWCNTs nanostructured network on a screen-printed electrode. The conductive scaffold provided an enlarged electroactive surface and facilitated interfacial charge transfer, whereas the molecular recognition cavities enabled selective rebinding of NFC and improved discrimination against matrix interferences. The synergistic integration of molecular recognition and signal transduction generated a sensitive analytical interface for NFC determination in processed extracts from complex food matrices. Under optimized conditions, the proposed sensor exhibited a linear concentration range of 0.16-25.00 µM, with a detection limit of 0.04 µM. The analytical applicability of the method was evaluated using fortified processed extracts of milk, egg, and shrimp, yielding recoveries of 90.1-107.0%, 91.6-106.0%, and 91.7-106.0%, respectively, with relative standard deviations below 8.9%. A limited comparison with HPLC showed no statistically significant differences for the milk extracts at all investigated concentrations or for the egg and shrimp extracts at 25.0 µM; however, significant differences were observed at lower concentrations in the egg and shrimp extracts. The proposed approach demonstrates the potential of molecular recognition cavity-based electrochemical sensing as a rapid, selective, and cost-effective strategy for screening NFC in processed food-sample extracts.

abstract: Oxidative phenol dearomatization using hypervalent iodine(III) reagents is a powerful tool for developing efficient synthetic routes to complex natural products and pharmaceuticals. This process enables the rapid formation of a functionalized dienone, a key intermediate derived from simple and inexpensive aromatic systems, thereby increasing structural complexity in a single step. Current methods, however, often require the use of perfluorinated alcohols as protic, non-nucleophilic solvents, which environmentally harmful nature deteriorates the green metrics of the reaction. This paper presents a solvent-free, mechanochemical methodology using a planetary ball mill to achieve the intramolecular oxidative dearomatization of several phenols that contain a heteronucleophile on a side chain. This process yields various spiranic systems within 5 min, with decent to good yields, and eliminates the need for expensive, environmentally harmful solvents. This approach has also been extended to a tandem Diels-Alder process and the first application of a bimolecular example. This paper thus introduces a greener strategy for dearomatizing phenols using hypervalent iodines, offering a more sustainable path for this widely used synthetic transformation.

abstract: Methyl iodide (CH<sub>3</sub>I) is the main organic carrier for iodine transport from both marine and terrestrial ecosystems into the atmosphere, playing an important role in the global iodine cycle and ozone depletion. The widespread input of heavy metal copper (Cu(II)) deposition in marine environments due to anthropogenic activities may affect the production of CH<sub>3</sub>I, yet relevant studies are still lacking. Here, we explored the effects of Cu(II) on emission of CH<sub>3</sub>I in coastal wetlands and seawater. The results showed that Cu(II) addition significantly enhances CH<sub>3</sub>I emission from coastal wetland soils, with emissions under hydrogen peroxide (H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) co-addition reaching approximately five times those observed with Cu(II) alone. Notably, this promotional effect was more pronounced in coastal wetland soils with higher organic matter content. In seawater, addition of 400 nM Cu(II) further stimulated the abiotic processes, with emission of CH<sub>3</sub>I increased 136% (day 8) in filtered seawater (biologically reduced). In unfiltered seawater, despite 400 nM Cu(II) addition inhibition of biological activity evidenced by an 81.7% decrease in chlorophyll-a and a 49.2% reduction in bacterial abundance, the overall CH<sub>3</sub>I emission was further amplified, which we tentatively attributed to the release of organic matter from the decay of phytoplankton. These findings elucidate that elevated copper stress promote CH<sub>3</sub>I emission from both salt marsh soil and ocean into the atmosphere. This study provides an important scientific basis for assessing the impact of heavy metal pollution on CH<sub>3</sub>I emissions from coastal wetlands and seawater under climate change scenarios and anthropogenic perturbations.

abstract: An efficient and highly selective photoredox/nickel dual-catalytic strategy has been developed for the synthesis of chiral allylic 1,3-diols bearing fully substituted quaternary stereocenters from readily available vinyl cyclic carbonates (VCCs) and aldehydes. The transformation proceeds through in situ generation of nucleophilic allyl-Ni intermediates, enabling regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselective coupling with aldehydes to deliver the desired products in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope, functional group tolerance, and scalability, providing versatile intermediates for downstream transformations without loss of stereochemical integrity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the reaction proceeds through a reductive quenching pathway and that a monomeric chiral Ni complex serves as the stereocontrol element. Collectively, these results address a long-standing challenge associated with the asymmetric construction of 1,3-diols bearing quaternary stereocenters.

abstract: Diborane(4) chemistry continues to reveal new aspects of the reactivity of electron-deficient p-block elements. These systems are capable of bond activation and ligand rearrangement-processes once thought to be exclusive to transition metals. Here, we show that reaction of B<sub>2</sub>Cat<sub>2</sub> (Cat = benzene-1,2-diolate) with mesityllithium (MesLi; Mes = 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl) affords an unusual 1,2-disubstituted diborane(4), Mes-B(μ-Cat)-B-Mes. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational data indicate that the catecholate co-ligand favors formation of the 1,2-isomer. Subsequent reaction with alcohols (ROH) cleaves the B─B bond in this compound to form CatBMes and MesB(OR)<sub>2</sub> via B(II) → B(III) oxidation, releasing H<sub>2</sub>. These results expand the reactive landscape of O,O-chelating diborane(4) systems, establish an entry into 1,2-diborane(4) frameworks, and demonstrate that their distinct reactivity toward alcohols can be exploited to differentiate the chemistry of 1,1- and 1,2-diborane(4) isomers.

abstract: Analytical chemistry, and particularly mass spectrometry (MS), plays a central role in the molecular characterization of biological and environmental samples. These data are essential for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying healthy aging, disease onset and progression, and the complex chemical composition of environmental systems. Over the past decades, MS has undergone unprecedented technological advancements. Current state-of-the-art instruments enable the  thorough characterization of deep proteomes at the single-cell level and achieve comprehensive coverage of metabolites and proteins. Innovations such as new mass analyzers (e.g., the Astral mass analyzer) and the integration of multidimensional separation techniques (e.g., trapped/cyclic ion mobility) have significantly expanded the analytical capabilities of the instrumentation. However, the volume and complexity of the data produced by these advanced platforms pose major challenges for interpretation and integration. To address these challenges, machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) methods are emerging as indispensable tools in analytical chemistry. These approaches, particularly deep learning, generative AI, and large language models, offer powerful solutions for analyzing, integrating, and interpreting the high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets generated in proteomics and metabolomics research. This chapter first introduces the fundamental principles and operational mechanisms of commonly used AI/ML methods in analytical chemistry. These include regression models, decision trees, k-nearest neighbors, support vector machines, neural networks, deep learning architectures, and generative AI. The first part of the chapter also discusses key requirements for model training, including the need for sufficient sample and molecular coverage, and evaluates how data noise affects model performance and reliability. In the second part, a series of representative applications are presented, demonstrating the use of AI/ML for peptide and metabolite observability prediction, retention time and ion mobility prediction, fragment ion spectrum generation, de novo compound identification, and improvements in compound quantification and scoring of identifications. The chapter concludes with practical recommendations for applying AI/ML approaches in proteomics and metabolomics studies, and for their integration into bioinformatics pipelines to enhance data interpretation, reproducibility, and scientific discovery.

abstract: Carbohydrate mimetics containing aromatic aglycone moieties have significant therapeutic potential, as they are able to inhibit lectins that play a key role in pathological processes such as cancer, inflammation, and bacterial infections. Glycomimetics containing isochroman and tryptoline aromatic aglycones have untapped potential in the field of lectin inhibition. We developed a general method for the preparation of thioglycoside-isochroman and thioglycoside-tryptoline conjugates from glycosyl thiols and phenethyl alcohol/tryptophan building blocks, by combining the oxa-Pictet-Spengler (oPS)/Pictet-Spengler (PS) cyclization method and the low-temperature photoinitiated thiol-ene coupling (cryo TEC) reaction. In our synthetic design, we used the bifunctional acrolein dimethyl acetal as a linker, which served as an oxo component in the oPS/PS reactions to form the desired heteroaromatic systems, and also exploited its double bond to conjugate thiosugars to the heterocyclic scaffold via cryo thio-click reaction, thus obtaining stable thioglycoside mimetics. The lectin-inhibitory properties of the novel galactose-, fucose- and mannose-containing glycomimetics were tested against Pseudomonas aeruginosa LecA and LecB lectins using competitive binding assays based on fluorescence polarization. STD NMR and molecular docking studies were performed to determine the epitope maps and the binding modes of the most potent compounds. Catechol-type isochroman-α-thioglycosides emerged as effective inhibitors of both LecA and LecB, while the tryptoline aglycone provided strong binding only to LecB.

abstract: Chemical ligation of polymer segments is an essential approach to extend the length of synthetic polymers. Ligating individual polymer chains at the molecular level remains a formidable challenge owing to the entropically disfavoured collision probability between reactive end groups, and the need to overcome the activation barrier. Here we report a pathway to chemical ligation of synthetic polymers via folding-driven supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation. Our strategy, which does not require thermal activation, uses hydrogen bonds that induce conformational folding to rigidify the polymer backbone while providing sticky ends for supramolecular pre-organization. This promotes base-catalysed covalent exchange between terminal groups (in our case, thiolate-disulfide groups). We obtain mechanistic insight in the ligation process by engineering side-chain units that determine conformational foldability and intermolecular H-bonding pre-organization. The resulting extended helical polymers fold into hierarchical globular architectures in solution and exhibit thermo-responsive macromolecular entanglements in bulk films. The combination of noncovalent assembly and dynamic covalent polymerization offers a supramolecular pathway for non-thermal and controllable polycondensation of dynamic polymers with secondary structures.

abstract: The chemical recycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into high-value terephthalic acid (TPA) under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we construct a dual-active-site Au/ATP catalyst via electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) by supporting Au on inexpensive attapulgite (ATP). Under optimal conditions (200 °C, 1 MPa Ar, 4 h), this catalyst achieves near-complete conversion of PET with a terephthalic acid (TPA) yield of 91.76 ± 1.65%, and is also effective for actual waste plastic bottle flakes. The EMSI stabilizes Au nanoparticles, modulates Lewis acidity to suppress side reactions, and enables selective ester-bond cleavage without affecting the benzene ring or CC bonds. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), work-function analysis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the EMSI effect drives electron transfer from Au to ATP, generating Au<sup>δ+</sup> species. These species can effectively polarize the CO bond to generate an electron-deficient intermediate. Meanwhile, ATP provides an adsorption and activation platform for H<sub>2</sub>O, promoting the generation of nucleophilic *OH. The synergy of these two sites enables highly performance depolymerization. This work provides a sustainable strategy for polyester chemical recycling and the value-added upgrading of low-grade mineral resources.

abstract: The removal of oil contaminants from water is a great challenge for sustainable wastewater treatment, clean water production, and environmental protection. Electrospun membranes based on cellulose acetate butyrate (CAB) were prepared for oil adsorption and oil/water separation in this study. The performance enhancers were hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), MIL-53(Al) metal-organic framework (MOF), and h-BN/MIL-53(Al) hybrid prepared by simple ultrasonication-assisted synthesis. The hybrid-containing membrane (CAB/1.5B1M) exhibited the highest oil adsorption capacity of 65.8 ± 2.6 g g<sup>-1</sup>, which was higher than those of neat CAB and the membranes only containing h-BN or MIL-53(Al). This improvement was attributed to the hybrid h-BN/MIL-53(Al) filler that induced a more open fibrous architecture and higher hydrophobicity, hence enhancing the oil uptake and retention. The adsorption capacity was increased by ~101% relative to the CAB membrane. The CAB/1.5B1M membrane adsorbed different oils on the solid and water surfaces and retained 73.5 ± 1.4% and 77.6 ± 3.1% of the initial adsorption capacities for soybean oil and used motor oil, respectively, after ten cycles. Furthermore, the membrane also enabled an effective gravity-driven separation of oil/water mixtures and water-in-oil emulsions, achieving a separation efficiency of 91.1% for diesel/water mixtures and no water was detected in the separated oil. The membrane could also wrap a hydrophilic sponge for pump-assisted separation and showed improved stress, strain, and toughness compared to neat CAB membrane. The results demonstrate a bio-based composite membrane platform for environmental remediation, oily wastewater treatment, and protection of aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

abstract: Nickel-catalyzed coupling reactions of propargylic compounds with nucleophiles or electrophiles have evolved into a powerful method for the preparation of propargylic compounds; however, it is still challenging for its regioselective formation of allenes. We herein report a mild nickel-catalyzed photoreduction of propargylic acetates enabling highly selective synthesis of 1,3-disubstituted and trisubstituted allenes with a broad functional group tolerance, and demonstrate its utility in preparing alkenyl boronic compounds and 1,3-dienes. Careful mechanistic studies unveiled that the protocol relies on a synergistic photoredox/nickel dual SET catalytic cycle, where N,N-diisopropylethylamine functions dually as the reductive quencher of the photocatalyst and the precursor of key α-aminoalkyl radicals, while water acts as the terminal H-atom donor. DFT calculations establish that the allene selectivity originates from a distortion-controlled Ni(II) protodemetalation. abstract: The emergence of life on our planet occurred somewhere before 3.48 billion years ago, and was predated by a poorly defined period of appearance and accumulation of chemical intermediates commonly known as biomolecules - which includes amino acids, lipids, sugars and components of genetic polymers. While no fossils are known to science from that period of Earth's development, prebiotic chemistry tried to experimentally answer the question: which chemical processes, and under which conditions, could provide our planet with biomolecules in sufficient quantity and structural diversity to enable spontaneous life formation. Here, we present a chronological overview of the hypotheses that have driven the development of prebiotic chemistry, and of seminal experiments which were intended to prove or disprove these hypotheses.

abstract: Click chemistry has transformed modern synthetic chemistry by providing efficient, selective, and modular strategies for constructing complex molecular structures. Since its introduction, the field has expanded from classical synthetic reactions to bioorthogonal and next-generation click platforms, broadening its applications across organic synthesis, polymer science, materials engineering, chemical biology, medicinal chemistry, and biomedicine. This review summarizes the evolution of click chemistry across three major generations. The first generation includes classical reactions such as copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC), thiol-ene, thiol-yne, thiol-ene Michael addition (TEMA), Diels-Alder (DA) cycloadditions, and nucleophilic ring-opening reactions. The second generation focuses on bioorthogonal transformations, including Strain-Promoted Alkyne-Azide Cycloaddition (SPAAC), Strain-Promoted Alkyne-Nitrone Cycloaddition (SPANC), and inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) reactions, which enable selective chemical modification in living systems. The third generation encompasses emerging platforms such as sulfur(vi) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) and phosphorus(v) fluoride exchange (PFEx), which provide enhanced structural tunability, external control, and broader application potential. For each reaction class, the review discusses fundamental mechanisms, key advantages, limitations, and representative applications, highlighting how click chemistry has evolved from efficient bond formation toward increasingly precise chemical control in biological and materials environments.

abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed annulation of diynes with nucleophiles is a powerful tool for constructing valuable complex (hetero)cycles. However, reports on the cascade annulation of diynes with dinucleophiles are rare and confined to noble-metal catalysts, narrow diyne scopes, and specific reaction types. Significantly, this protocol represents the first non-noble-metal-catalyzed annulation of diynes with dinucleophiles.

abstract: Biofilm phototherapy is constrained by therapeutic reach, as light-triggered damage is often concentrated near accessible regions while bacteria remain protected within the extracellular matrix. Here we report wavelength-division Janus nanomotors for access-gated biofilm phototherapy, in which asymmetric interfacial energy conversion and wavelength-resolved activation couple active transport with antibacterial action. Janus SiO<sub>2</sub>/Au/FeTAPP nanomotors (JSAF) combine asymmetric Au and FeTAPP functional domains on dendritic porous silica nanoparticles. Under 808 nm irradiation, the asymmetric Au domain enables 808 nm-responsive active motion consistent with self-thermophoretic transport and contributes to heat-assisted matrix traversal. In mature biofilms, JSA exhibits enhanced penetration and a broader depth distribution than a symmetric SiO<sub>2</sub>/Au photothermal control, indicating that photothermal matrix disruption alone does not fully reproduce the transport behavior of the Janus architecture. Under 630 nm irradiation, FeTAPP generates singlet oxygen for localized oxidative bacterial killing. Order-dependent irradiation supports an access-first, killing-second relationship, whereas combined dual-wavelength activation enables a continuous access-to-killing process as particle transport progressively extends localized oxidative action into deeper biofilm regions. This wavelength-addressed coupling reduces residual biofilm biomass and improves healing of S. aureus-infected wounds. These findings highlight interfacial asymmetry and wavelength-selective functional coupling as design principles for active colloids operating in transport-limited environments.

abstract: The oxaliplatin-based therapy regimens for colorectal cancer (CRC) presents a significant challenge to clinical application owing to the severe side effects and drug resistance. To enhance the selectivity and therapeutic efficacy of oxaliplatin, we designed and synthesized a series of platinum (IV) prodrugs by conjugating NF-κB inhibitor EF24 analogs to an oxaliplatin -derived platinum (IV) complex. Among them, the platinum (IV) prodrug 6d demonstrated the most potent inhibitory effect on HCT-116/Oxa cells, 4T1 cells and CT26 cells in both in vitro and in vivo compared to oxaliplatin. Mechanistic studies indicated that 6d could induce significant DNA damage and suppress the MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, ultimately leading to CRC cell death. Especially, 6d induced cell death by promoting autophagy through suppressing the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and suppressed the expression of PD-L1. More importantly, 6d triggered autophagy to mediate immunogenic cell death (ICD) effect both in vitro and in vivo, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. These findings indicate that 6d may represent a potential chemotherapeutic candidate for the treatment of CRC.

abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as nanocarriers for biomedical applications. However, their performance under physiological conditions is strongly governed by framework degradation processes occurring at the crystal-solution interface. Here, we systematically investigate the role of surface functionalization in controlling the stability and cargo-release behavior of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) nanoparticles. ZIF-8 surfaces were modified with polyethylene glycol (PEG) derivatives bearing hydroxyl, amino, and imidazole end groups, enabling comparison of different anchoring strategies involving coordinative and covalent interactions. Framework stability, surface modification, and fluorescein release as a model cargo system were evaluated using FTIR spectroscopy, XRPD, STEM, TGA, and UV-vis spectroscopy. Although PEGylation reduced fluorescein release in phosphate-buffered saline compared with unmodified ZIF-8 nanoparticles, the influence of the anchoring group was minimal, demonstrating that PEG coatings provide only limited protection against phosphate-induced surface degradation. To further elucidate the role of interfacial bonding, fluorescein derivatives directly attached to the ZIF-8 framework were investigated as molecular probes of surface stability. While the bonding mode affected dye retention in pure water, this stabilization effect was largely suppressed under phosphate-containing conditions. These results reveal the complex interplay between surface chemistry, framework degradation, and cargo release, providing design considerations for the development of MOF-based biomedical carriers.

abstract: A palladium-catalyzed Freon-to-carbonyl transfer strategy has been developed for the CO-free aminocarbonylation of aryl and heteroaryl iodides with amines. Using chlorodifluoromethane (Freon-22) as both a difluorocarbene precursor and a carbonyl source, this protocol enables direct access to diverse benzamide derivatives without external CO gas or conventional CO-releasing reagents. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional-group tolerance, accommodating electronically diverse aryl iodides, polycyclic and heteroaryl iodides, and primary and secondary amines. Its synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage benzamidation of bioactive-molecule-derived substrates and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant benzamide scaffolds, including trimethobenzamide and methyl tamibarotene. Mechanistic experiments involving benzimidazole trapping and H218O labeling support a difluorocarbene-derived carbonyl-transfer process in which water contributes to the oxygen atom of the amide carbonyl group. This work establishes Freon-22 as a practical carbonyl surrogate for CO-free amide synthesis.

abstract: Seventeen undescribed triterpenoids, comprising three structural types-protostanes (1-5), multifloranes (6-8), and oleanane analogs (10-18), along with eight known compounds (9, and 19-25), were isolated from the leaves of Alangium salviifolium, a plant of the genus Alangium (family Cornaceae). Their structures were elucidated through extensive NMR and HRESIMS analyses, and the absolute configurations of 1a, 6, 7, 10, and 11 were confirmed by X-ray diffraction. Interestingly, compound 1 underwent an intramolecular electrophilic addition to form derivative 1a spontaneously. Bioactivity evaluation demonstrated that compounds 11, 19, 20, 22, and 24 significantly inhibited nitric oxide (NO) production in LPS-induced RAW264.7 cells, with 19 showing the most potent activity. Further investigation confirmed that 19 alleviated LPS-induced inflammation in macrophages and lung injury in mice by modulating the AKT/MAPK pathway. These findings underscore the potential of A. salviifolium leaves as a source of anti-inflammatory agents.

abstract: Cancer remains a major global health threat. Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has revolutionized the modulation of protein function in therapeutic development. Nevertheless, the design of current TPD agents continues to face challenges, including hook effects and, more critically, the frequent lack of spatial and temporal precision required for in vivo applications. Herein, we report a photoactivatable targeted degradation (PATD) strategy and describe the iterative optimization of compound 9, the first two-photon-excited BRD4 photodegrader, achieved through molecular engineering of the photosensitizer core, auxiliary ligands, and linkers. Notably, BRD4 degradation downregulates GPX4 transcription, promoting lipid peroxidation and thereby inducing ferro-aging, while simultaneously triggering chemo-aging via histone H3 cleavage, which leads to DNA damage and cell cycle arrest. This dual-aging mechanism accelerates tumor cell senescence, enabling synergistic seno-immunotherapy. Beyond conventional photosensitizers that primarily elicit immunogenic cell death (ICD) alone, complex 9 integrates senescence-driven immunity with ICD-mediated antitumor immunity. This combined immunostimulatory strategy elicits robust systemic antitumor responses and achieves amplified therapeutic efficacy in patient-derived organoids (PDOs), presenting a new paradigm for precision targeted protein degradation in therapy-resistant tumors.

abstract: Based on a recently developed screening approach for the analysis of mineral oil saturated and mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons (MOSH and MOAH) in lipid-rich food matrix (vegetable oil) using silver ion planar solid phase extraction with ultraviolet/fluorescence detection (Ag-pSPE-UV/FLD), an approach was developed for dry food samples with low fat content. Different fluorescent dyes were investigated for MOSH detection, and berberine was identified as the best humidity-independent option. The performance criteria calculated for the Ag-pSPE-UV/FLD method were a decision limit (L<sub>C</sub>) of 0.10 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>, a detection limit (LOD) of 0.20 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>, and a quantification limit (LOQ) of 0.36 mg kg<sup>-1</sup> for MOSH, with recoveries around 91%. For MOAH, the L<sub>C</sub> was calculated to be 0.03 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>, the LOD was 0.05 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>, and the LOQ 0.08 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>, with recoveries around 96%. As an additional option, the pSPE was hyphenated with gas chromatography-flame ionization detection (GC-FID). For quantification using Ag-pSPE-GC-FID, suitable internal standards were identified with squalane for MOSH and o-terphenyl for MOAH quantification. LOD and LOQ for MOSH were calculated to be 0.13 and 0.42 mg kg<sup>-1</sup><sub>,</sub> respectively and for MOAH, LOD and LOQ were determined to be 0.11 and 0.35 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>, respectively. Quantification of dry food samples using Ag-pSPE-UV/FLD and Ag-pSPE-GC-FID yielded results similar to those of the routine LC-GC-FID method.

abstract: Norcantharidin (NCTD), a semi-synthetic derivative of cantharidin from the animal-derived traditional Chinese medicine Cantharides, was selected as a potential functional anticancer ligand. Then three new Pt(IV) complexes (Pt-NCTD-bu, Pt-NCTD-pe, Pt-NCTD-he) were designed as a homologous series to evaluate how increasing axial chain length affects lipophilicity and anticancer efficacy. The axial carboxylate ligands were employed to modulate lipophilicity and coordination stability. These complexes exhibited stronger cytotoxicity against the most sensitive A2780 cells than cisplatin, with the order of potency following he > pe > bu, correlating with increasing lipophilicity and cellular uptake. All three complexes also effectively suppressed colony formation. They also overcame cisplatin resistance in A2780/CDDP cells. Mechanistically, they could release active Pt(II) and NCTD via GSH-mediated reduction, inducing ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage and cell apoptosis. Especially, under intracellular hypoxia condition, Pt-NCTD-he showed the highest oxygen-independent cytotoxicity. In vivo, Pt-NCTD-he (20 mg/kg) more effectively suppressed tumor growth in A2780 xenografts than cisplatin, with a 70.0% inhibition rate. Pt-NCTD-he was found to mainly distribute in the liver, indicating that a higher lipophilicity is conducive to better anticancer activity. Pt-NCTD-he also showed satisfactory pharmacokinetic properties, with a longer elimination half-life (1.3 h) than cisplatin (ca. 0.5 h). This work highlights the rational design of Pt(IV) complexes by integrating natural medicinal ingredients, providing a promising strategy for the new generation of Pt(IV)-based complexes as anticancer prodrugs.

abstract: Organoboron compounds are versatile building blocks for C─C and C-heteroatom bond formation, with broad applications in drug discovery and materials science. Hydroboration of alkenes with hydroboranes is a reliable route to access organoboron compoundsssssss, yet the Markovnikov-selective hydroboration of unactivated terminal alkenes remains challenging. In this study, we report a triple catalysis strategy for the highly Markovnikov-selective hydroboration of unactivated terminal alkenes with HBaza-type hydroborane (HBaza: 1,3,2-benzodiazaborolane). The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional group compatibility, and has been successfully applied to the Markovnikov hydroboration of alkene derivatives from complex molecules. Further derivatizations of the resulting alkyl boron products, as well as the synthesis of biologically relevant molecules or intermediates, highlight the synthetic value of this method. Mechanistic studies support that this reaction proceeds via sequential metal-hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated radical generation and HBaza-involved radical borylation process under a triple photoredox, cobalt, and Brønsted acid catalysis.

abstract: Thermoresponsive injectable hydrogels are promising platforms for soft tissue repair because they enable minimally invasive administration and undergo sol-gel transition under physiological conditions. In this study, methylcellulose-based hydrogels were prepared using sodium sulfate as a thermogelation-promoting agent and functionalized with thiolated hyaluronic acid (HA-SH) and a β-cyclodextrin/curcumin (β-CD/CUR) inclusion complex. The β-CD/CUR complex improved curcumin compatibility and dispersion within the aqueous hydrogel matrix. All formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, supporting injectability, while qualitative self-healing tests showed recovery of structural continuity after mechanical disruption. HA-SH incorporation altered the hydration and porous structure, increasing water uptake while reducing porosity. CUR-loaded hydrogels provided sustained curcumin release under physiological conditions, reaching 67.94 ± 6.52% after 24 h for MC3.5/1.5-HA0.25/CUR0.5, with diffusion modeling indicating a diffusion-controlled mechanism. The released curcumin retained antioxidant activity, with the highest DPPH radical scavenging observed at the highest CUR loading. All hydrogels were cytocompatible with normal human fibroblasts, maintaining viability above 80% throughout the study and exceeding 100% after 72 h. CUR-loaded formulations also showed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, with MC3.5/1.5-HA0.25/CUR0.5 exhibiting the strongest effect. IL-1β analysis showed no pronounced pro-inflammatory response, while CUR-loaded hydrogels reduced LPS-induced IL-1β secretion over time. Scratch assays further demonstrated enhanced fibroblast-mediated wound closure, particularly after 24 and 48 h. Overall, these HA-SH/CUR-loaded thermoresponsive hydrogels combine injectability, cytocompatibility, controlled release, antioxidant and antibacterial activity, and wound closure-supporting properties, highlighting their potential as bioactive platforms for various biomedical applications.

abstract: The concurrent detection of multiple thalassemia mutations remains challenging due to the limitations of conventional single-readout biosensors in terms of reliability and sensitivity. Herein, we report an intelligent photoelectrochemical (PEC)/colorimetric dual-mode biosensor that integrates an OR logic gate with a DNAzyme Walker cascade amplification strategy, built on a proposed Z-scheme Bi2S3/Bi-BiOI heterojunction whose proposed Z-scheme charge-transfer pathway is supported by Mott-Schottky and photovoltage measurements. The OR logic gate enables parallel recognition of CD142 and CD41-42 mutations, outputting a unified trigger to initiate a nicking enzyme-assisted DNAzyme Walker. This autonomous machinery releases abundant G-quadruplex/hemin (G4-hemin) complexes, serving as a bifunctional signal transducer. Notably, the specific binding of G4-hemin to the electrode interface induces a distinct anodic-to-cathodic photocurrent polarity switching, which, coupled with its intrinsic peroxidase-mimicking activity, allows for self-validated dual-signal output. The platform achieves limits of detection down to 28.7 aM (PEC) and 2.6 fM (colorimetric) across a wide linear range (0.1 fM-0.1 μM). Furthermore, the dual-mode design effectively eliminates false positives through signal cross-validation. Practical application in human serum yielded satisfactory recoveries (94.1-107.8%), highlighting the platform's potential for high-precision genetic screening in resource-limited settings.

abstract: Organic chemistry sits at a pivotal moment. Two decades after combinatorial chemistry promised to industrialize molecule making, the field has converged on a far more interesting reality: medicinal chemists now operate at the intersection of new catalytic paradigms, biological-scale automation, machine learning, and an expanding set of therapeutic modalities that look very little like the flat aromatic scaffolds of the 1990s. This Perspective surveys the dominant trends shaping contemporary organic synthesis in the context of drug discovery-late-stage C─H functionalization, photoredox and electrochemical catalysis, biocatalysis, continuous flow manufacturing, AI-guided retrosynthesis, DNA-encoded libraries (DELs), and proximity-based modalities such as PROTACs and molecular glues-and discusses how their convergence is redefining how molecules are designed, made, and validated. The future of the discipline lies not in any single breakthrough, but in the controlled integration of these threads into closed-loop, data-rich, and increasingly autonomous discovery pipelines. We also identify open challenges: predictability of complex sp<sup>3</sup>-rich scaffolds, scalability of new modalities, environmental footprint, and the need for chemistry education and infrastructure to keep pace with computational advances.

abstract: Understanding how structural modifications control the electronic and supramolecular behavior of hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene (HBC) nanographenes remains a central challenge in π-conjugated materials design. Here, we demonstrate that variation of a central sp<sup>3</sup>-C substituent in tris-HBC(tBu)<sub>5</sub> nanographenes modulates the electronic structure through combined through-bond and through-space effects. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a pronounced substituent-size dependence on supramolecular organization. The ─CH<sub>3</sub> derivative assembles exclusively via π-π stacking into well-separated two-dimensional parallel layers with one-dimensional channels. In contrast, the ─H analogue adopts offset antiparallel layered assemblies driven by cooperative π-π and C─H⋯arene edge contacts, bringing adjacent layers into closer proximity. Notably, solvent-mediated hydrogen-bonding induces a distinct layered arrangement in the ─OH analogue. The bulkier ─OCH<sub>3</sub> and ─OC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub> substituents disrupt this packing motif, with only two HBC units participating in intermolecular π-π stacking, while the third engages in C─H⋯π interactions with a differently oriented neighboring unit, leading to a different packing arrangement. Consistent with these structural differences, systematic variations in redox potentials, photophysical responses, excited-state lifetimes, and vibrational features are observed, in good agreement with density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations. Overall, central sp<sup>3</sup> substitution provides an effective strategy for tuning structure-property relationships in tris-HBC nanographenes.
