abstract: It is remarkably attractive but challenging to develop fine Pt-rare-earth intermetallic catalysts toward efficient and stable oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) for fuel cell applications. In this work, an amino-assisted method was employed to prepare the carbon-supported Pt5Sm (Pt5Sm/C) catalyst, which exhibited an average size of 3.8 ± 1.0 nm with a core-shell structure consisting of a Pt-enriched surface over a hexagonal Pt5Sm intermetallic core. The introduction of Sm into the Pt lattice induced strong electron interactions between Sm and Pt and enhanced the resistance to Pt oxidation, thereby improving the catalytic kinetics and durability for the ORR. In rotating disk electrode tests, the Pt5Sm/C catalyst delivers a promising ORR activity of 430.3 A·gPt-1 with only a 10.3% loss after 30,000 cycles, significantly outperforming commercial Pt/C. Furthermore, in H2/air fuel cell tests, the Pt5Sm/C catalyst exhibited a peak power density of 853 mW·cm-2 with only a voltage drop of 56 mV at 0.8 A·cm-2 after 30,000 cycles. This work demonstrates that Pt-rare-earth intermetallic catalysts are promising candidates for high-performance and durable fuel cell applications.

abstract: Following the changes in the conditions of water resources and the challenges of water shortage, water resources management is considered more important. Accordingly, the use of the traditional water balance approach that focuses on the balance of water input and output in a system has been replaced with newer methods such as water accounting. Providing a more comprehensive and accurate picture of water flows and uses, water accounting enables more efficient management of water resources. Doing water accounting manually can be associated with many challenges. One of the challenges is the need for computer knowledge to download satellite images. Additionally, the large amount of calculations needed for water accounting usually leads to calculation errors, affecting negatively the validity of the results. Model calibration is also a time-consuming process that requires a lot of concentration and precision. Moreover, analyzing satellite images for water accounting purposes through common software such as ArcGIS can be very difficult and time-consuming. Although these software are powerful, they are not developed specifically for water accounting. Therefore, it is necessary to provide dedicated software that facilitates the water accounting process. The present paper introduces the water accounting plus software called Aquametrics Plus. This software has been provided to improve the capabilities of users who face the mentioned challenges when using the WA+ framework. To investigate the performance and accuracy of the software, a case study has been conducted on the Zayandehrood basin. In this research, the results indicated that the use of software increased the speed of calculations, saved time, reduced calculation errors, and increased the precision of calibration and calculations.

This position paper introduces young carers as a key stakeholder within AI. Research on AI for health care endeavors to assist and optimize current health care services; yet, young carers have been neglected thus far. Accordingly, this paper situates itself at the intersection of young people under the age of 18 years old providing care (referred to as young carers) and AI research. Through a socio-legal and public health lens, this paper (1) situates young carers to showcase (2) why they must be accounted for in AI systems, and (3) how AI researchers can do so. This lens highlights the difficulties young carers tend to face at present and how AI systems can alleviate those-rather than reproduce them. Accordingly, we rely on the norms-in-the-loop framework to demonstrate why the AI community must account for young carers in AI systems. We first synthesize research on both young carers and AI research on contextual, legal, and social norms to then propose practical ways to do so through design, datasets, and in situ personalization. Overall, this paper offers a critical foundation for AI researchers to include young carers in the development of AI systems at various levels: from institutions to care receivers, and to young carers themselves. Ultimately, this paper posits that young carers must be identified and supported, which demands their inclusion in AI research to understand how best to do so. Accounting for young carers will allow for their unique perspectives to be reflected in AI systems and help them thrive beyond their care responsibilities.

abstract: Shallow lake wetlands have important vegetation and soil carbon pools; yet, habitat-level differences in carbon storage among lake types have been insufficiently quantified. In this study, we compared three representative shallow lake wetlands in eastern China, Qin Lake, Changdang Lake, and Hongze Lake, during low- and high-water periods. We combined Sentinel-2-based land-cover classification with field measurements to distinguish aquatic vegetation functional types and to estimate vegetation carbon density, surface soil organic carbon density, and combined vegetation-surface soil organic carbon storage. The three lakes showed distinct habitat composition and carbon-storage structures. Qin Lake had the highest proportion of emergent vegetation, Changdang Lake had the highest proportion of floating-leaved vegetation, and Hongze Lake was dominated by open water with relatively strong aquaculture disturbance. Under the biomass-accounting scheme adopted in this study, emergent vegetation showed the highest estimated vegetation carbon density and generally made a relatively high contribution to the estimated vegetation carbon pool, whereas surface soil carbon dominated the combined carbon pool, accounting for 69.82%-93.93% of total estimated storage. Period-averaged combined carbon storage was 8.75, 85.70, and 1023 kt C in Qin Lake, Changdang Lake, and Hongze Lake, respectively. Between the low- and high-water periods, the combined carbon storage was estimated to be lower in Qin Lake and Hongze Lake but higher in Changdang Lake, reflecting differences in habitat composition and habitat-specific carbon density. These results illustrate the value of habitat-level and functional-type-based carbon accounting for interpreting carbon-storage heterogeneity in shallow lake wetlands.

abstract: Public agencies may use machine learning to prioritize records for review before investigation or adjudication, but enforcement labels are selective, delayed, and legally ambiguous. This study develops a law-aware, interpretable system for ranking U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) 10-K and 10-Q filing periods according to later issuer-level Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Release (AAER) association. The reviewed panel contains 331,388 observations from 14,047 firms and 904 positives. Models are trained on fiscal years 2009–2018, selected on 2019–2020, and evaluated on an outcome-mature 2021–2022 cohort containing 51,627 observations and 123 positives. An adaptive neural model learns context-dependent lower and upper accounting thresholds and converts deviations into reviewable exceedance contributions. It achieves ROC-AUC 0.7569 and PR-AUC 0.01244, compared with 0.6837 and 0.00709 for logistic regression. The issuer-clustered ROC-AUC difference is 0.0733 (95% confidence interval 0.0224–0.1265; bootstrap p = 0.012), while PR-AUC and fixed-budget recall differences remain uncertain. Calibration, seed stability, firm-disjoint testing, annual-filing retraining, ablations, and label-horizon analyses limit the predictive claim. The article then derives governance requirements for administrative triage: purpose limitation, independent human judgment, reviewability, audit logs, correction, access control, and monitoring of drift and selective-label feedback. The score is a confidential prioritization aid, not evidence of fraud, liability, or any legal violation.

abstract:
Purpose This study examines whether accounting earnings are converted into sustainable dividends and realized shareholder wealth. It identifies when earnings retention becomes unjustified, when distributions exceed cash-supported capacity, and how allocation misalignment affects firm value and shareholder returns. Design/methodology/approach: The study uses an unbalanced panel of 67 non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian Exchange during 2015–2025, comprising 706 firm-year observations. It develops a Sustainable Dividend Capacity Index, a Profit Allocation Alignment Gap, and a Profit Allocation Transparency Index. Firm and year fixed-effects models, fractional-response and dynamic-panel estimations, content analysis, and an event study of 327 clean ex-dividend events are complemented by endogeneity, robustness, and matched-market tests.

Findings:

Earnings quality significantly strengthens sustainable dividend capacity (β = 0.271, p < 0.01), but reported profit does not automatically create shareholder wealth. Both over-retention and over-distribution reduce total shareholder return and firm value. Allocation-aligned observations achieve the highest mean shareholder return (19.8%). Transparency and governance mitigate the valuation cost of misalignment, market repricing partially transmits this cost, and economic uncertainty amplifies it. Originality/value: The study reconceptualizes dividend policy as accountable profit allocation rather than a payout-ratio decision. Its three measures distinguish productive retention from over-retention and sustainable dividends from financially excessive distributions, thereby explaining how accounting profit becomes—or fails to become—shareholder wealth. Theoretical, practical and social implications: The findings integrate agency, signalling, free-cash-flow, life-cycle, and institutional perspectives around allocation alignment. They support a “Distribute or Explain” framework and a dedicated Profit Allocation Report. These mechanisms can strengthen board accountability, minority-shareholder protection, and market confidence without imposing a uniform payout requirement.

abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) storage projects are an increasingly prominent natural climate solution, drawing investment from diverse climate-sensitive stakeholders. However, the OC additions that build SOC can alter emissions of the potent greenhouse gas (GHG) nitrous oxide (N2O). These emission changes can erode the intended GHG benefit when OC inputs fuel spatiotemporally episodic hot spots and hot moments (HSHM), which can dominate annual N2O emission budgets. Concerningly, HSHM are systematically under-quantified by the emission factors and process-based models that most SOC protocols rely on. This creates a poorly quantified risk to the demonstrable net climate benefit of SOC projects. To address this, we make two novel contributions. First, we introduce an assessment framework that scores the probability of project-induced N2O increases across distinct domains that are typically conflated in existing frameworks. One domain of the score characterizes N2O risk based on site and SOC intervention practices while the other evaluates the adequacy of N2O emission measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification (MMRV) under the protocol being applied. Second, we propose that credit retirement be linked to the composite N2O risk score so that N2O emissions are explicitly factored into SOC accounting protocols. We close with a research-to-practice agenda that proposes two parallel sets of objectives. The first is protocol performance trials, wherein crediting workflows are run under intensive direct field measurements to empirically characterize N2O accounting accuracy in current protocols. The second is development of direct measurements that comprise “minimum viable MMRV” for robust N2O accounting in SOC projects right now. Our proposed activities will help prevent the establishment of crediting systems that retire GHG credits that are not representative of true CO2-equivalent offsets. Rigorous accounting of N2O in SOC projects must become a shared responsibility of the research community, project developers, buyers, and registries.

abstract:
Objective

To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of imported malaria cases in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region from 2017 to 2024, so as to formulate the targeted control strategies for imported malaria.

Methods

The demographic and epidemiological data of malaria cases reported in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region from 2017 to 2024 were collected through the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System. The source of malaria cases acquiring infections, composition of malaria parasite species, regional distribution of malaria cases, population characteristics of malaria cases, temporal distribution of malaria cases, time of diagnosis, deaths and institutions reporting malaria cases were statistically analyzed with a descriptive statistical method.

Results

A total of 1 308 malaria cases were reported in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region from 2017 to 2024, and all cases were overseas imported cases, with no secondary cases identified. Plasmodium falciparum malaria (57.11%, 747/1 308) and P. ovale malaria (27.68%, 362/1 308) were two most common forms of malaria, and three deaths occurred among P. falciparum malaria cases. The number of malaria cases appeared an overall tendency towards a decline from 2017 to 2022, followed by a rise after 2023. The malaria cases predominantly acquired infections from Africa (1 284 cases, accounting for 98.17%), with Ghana (432 cases, accounting for 33.03%) and Cameroon (145 cases, accounting for 11.09%) as two most frequent origin countries, and P. falciparum malaria (58.02%, 745/1 284) was the predominant form of malaria among African imported malaria cases; however, P. vivax malaria cases comprised 89.58% (86/96) of all malaria cases derived from Ethiopia. In terms of regional distribution, malaria cases were highly concentrated in Nanning City (1 075 cases, accounting for 82.19%), with the most prominent situated in Shanglin County (903 cases, accounting for 69.04%), and these cases were predominantly found among individuals at ages of 20 to 59 years (1 280 cases, accounting for 97.86%), males (1 265 cases, accounting for 96.71%), and gold/coal mining workers (1 042 cases, accounting for 79.66%). In terms of temporal distribution, malaria cases were reported throughout the year, with the peak incidence in April (146 cases, accounting for 11.16%). The median duration from onset of disease to initial diagnosis was 1 (interquartile range, 2) day, and the median duration from initial diagnosis to definitive diagnosis was 1 (interquartile range, 1) day. Malaria cases were predominantly reported by medical institutions (1 075 cases, accounting for 82.19%), and the proportion of malaria cases reported by medical institutions increased from 75.92% in 2017 to 96.27% in 2024, while the proportion of malaria cases reported by disease control and prevention institutions reduced from 24.08% in 2017 to 3.73% in 2024. There was a significant difference in the proportion of malaria cases reported by medical institutions and disease control and prevention institutions from 2017 to 2024 (both P < 0.001). The 3 dead imported P. falciparum malaria cases predominantly received initial diagnosis at townshipand lower-level institutions (66.67%, 2/3), with 1 (interquartile range, 2) day median duration from onset of disease to initial diagnosis, 2 (interquartile range, 4) days median duration from initial diagnosis to definitive diagnosis, and 1 (interquartile range, 19) day median duration from definitive diagnosis to death.

Conclusions

Imported P. falciparum malaria from Africa is predominant among malaria cases in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, and malaria cases are highly concentrated in specific regions and among specific occupational groups. It is recommended to strengthen inter-departmental collaboration, implement refined management among labors going to Africa, improve the integration of medical treatment and disease prevention, and enhance the diagnosis and treatment of severe malaria cases.

abstract: Enterprise hardware refresh cycles generate significant volumes of electronic waste and poorly evidenced Scope 3 emissions. Conventional IT Asset Disposition (ITAD) workflows depend on off-site processing centres, introducing multi week turnaround delays and data-exposure risk during transit of unsanitised storage media. Concurrently, commercial ESG accounting platforms predominantly rely on spend-based emission factors that cannot reflect the physical condition of the asset being retired. This paper presents Eco-ITAD, an on-premise diagnostic and carbon accounting engine implemented in Python and Flask. The system derives a deterministic composite health score from NVMe S.M.A.R.T. endurance telemetry, memory subsystem capacity, and normalised compute capability, and maps this score to avoided embodied emissions using a remaining- service-life allocation model parameterised with UK DEFRA conversion factors and published lifecycle inventory data. Com- pliance certificates are generated entirely in volatile memory using buffered I/O streams, incorporating SHA-256 integrity digests while eliminating persistent audit artifacts on host storage. Evaluated across 50 executions on an enterprise desktop system (AMD64 Family 23 Model 113, 31.9 GB RAM, 1 TB Samsung SSD 860 EVO), the diagnostic pipeline achieved mean completion time of 0.322 s (σ = 0.007 s), peak single-core CPU utilization of 103.2%, and zero persistent writes to host storage. We additionally report a sensitivity analysis of the carbon model and an explicit discussion of the limitations of proxy-based health estimation.

abstract:
Purpose:

This study examines whether voluntary environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure improves the financial performance of commercial banks in an emerging market, and whether the effect differs between accounting-based and market-based performance. Design/methodology. Using an unbalanced panel of Vietnamese commercial banks over 2010–2025, we construct a voluntary ESG disclosure index from annual and sustainability reports through content analysis across the environmental, social, and governance pillars. Financial performance is captured by two accounting measures (ROA, ROE) and two market measures (Tobin’s Q, price-to-book). We estimate fixed-effects models for the accounting measures and random-effects models for the market measures, based on F, Breusch–Pagan and Hausman tests, with bank-clustered robust standard errors; we address multicollinearity through a reduced-form specification and endogeneity through a two-step system GMM estimator. Findings. Voluntary ESG disclosure is positively and significantly associated with accounting performance—most strongly with ROE (β = 0.0021, p < 0.01)—and the effect on ROA becomes significant once multicollinearity between disclosure, size and age is mitigated. In contrast, ESG disclosure shows no significant association with either market measure. The positive effect on accounting performance is confirmed by a dynamic system-GMM estimator that controls for endogeneity. Leverage, bank age, liquidity, media pressure and CEO stability are additional determinants of accounting performance. Originality/value. The study provides among the first long-window (16-year) evidence for a frontier banking market and documents a disclosure–performance asymmetry: banks are rewarded in their books but not (yet) in their market valuation, indicating that the capital market has not yet fully priced sustainability transparency.

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in corporate reporting, where accounting policies and estimates require professional judgment. This conceptual study examines how GenAI may assist preparers without displacing human responsibility or reinforcing managerial bias. Using theory adaptation, it integrates research on professional judgment, motivated reasoning and automation reliance. It identifies five bias-amplification mechanisms: anchoring, automation bias, outcome-directed prompting, unverified justification and diffusion of responsibility. The paper develops TRACE, a proposed framework comprising task boundary, regulatory grounding, alternative assessment, challenge and contradiction, and evidence trail. Its intended operation is illustrated through four constructed IFRS cases covering IAS 8 and IAS 16, IAS 36, IAS 37 and IFRS 15, three involving climate-transition assumptions. The AI proposals are stylised illustrations, not actual model outputs or empirical data. The analysis suggests that GenAI is most defensible when used to identify alternatives and contradictory evidence and to challenge a preferred treatment, and least defensible when asked to select or justify a conclusion. TRACE may make AI-assisted judgments more attributable and contestable, but it cannot guarantee unbiased or technically correct outcomes; independent human review remains necessary. The framework has not been empirically validated. It considers governance, control, reporting reliability and sustainable management.

abstract:
Introduction

Information asymmetry between bank managers and external stakeholders is a common relationship between financial-statement fraud and banking instability.

Methods

This study combines an AI-augmented forensic accounting framework with voluntary disclosure, banking stability indicators, and exploratory machine learning (ML) approaches. The study integrates fixed-effects regression with Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Isolation Forest, and SHAP-based explainability using panel data from the whole population of seven banks listed on the Palestine Exchange (2019-2025).

Results

According to the econometric results, there is a conditional rather than a uniform relationship between voluntary disclosure and financial stability, with variation by bank size, age, and leverage. Additionally, the exploratory machine-learning analyses indicate that nonlinear approaches could help find unusual bank-year records and instability-risk patterns that are not fully captured by traditional linear models. SHAP analysis enhanced the interpretability of model classifications, and ensemble approaches outperformed Logistic Regression in cross-validation within this small sample. The machine-learning results are considered as exploratory proof-of-concept evidence rather than externally confirmed predictive outcomes due to the small sample size and lack of independently verified fraud labels.

Discussion

Overall, the study shows how AI-augmented forensic accounting can enhance supervisory prioritization, instability-risk screening, and the expert assessment of anomalous observations in institutionally unstable banking contexts, thereby complementing traditional econometric analysis.

abstract: Microplastics (MPs), mostly stemming from terrestrial activities, can be easily transported once they enter freshwater. Limited national-level accounting has constrained accurate global estimates, investigations of environmental fate, and the development of targeted management measures for MP pollution. In this context, this study estimated MP generation and its release into freshwater in China from 2000 to 2022, with a focus on 21 typical inland activities and products. An accumulation of 6.36 × 1021 MPs (36.39 million tonnes, Mt) was generated, of which 2.39 × 1021 items (20.12 Mt) were released into freshwater, equivalent to 1.82 trillion and 1.01 trillion 20-g plastic bottles, respectively. Urban and rural areas made distinct contributions to MP generation, with urban areas contributing a greater quantity (59.12%) and rural areas contributing a greater mass (79.60%). The most critical contributors to MP generation and freshwater release were identified as transportation-related sources by number (>99.9%) and agricultural sources by mass (>59.9%). This study provides a methodological basis for MP accounting, especially in areas lacking monitoring capabilities, and helps identify effective and efficient MP control strategies.

abstract: The purpose of this research was to identify how the application of collaborative learning could support enhancing analytical skills of first-year undergraduate financial accounting students at a South African University. It has become increasingly important for the accounting industry and larger 21st-century work force to have individuals with strong analytical thinking capabilities; therefore, it is necessary to develop new ways of teaching that go beyond the traditional lecture-based format especially in the first year of post-secondary education when foundational competences are established. Data collection occurred using a qualitative case-study methodology; therefore, data was obtained from three different sources. Those sources include: (1) Focus Group Discussions; (2) Classroom Observations; and (3) Reflective Journals to obtain insight into students' perceptions regarding their experience with collaborative learning within an introductory Financial Accounting Course. The position of this study was grounded on the premise of Sustainability; therefore, collaborative learning was positioned as a low-cost, socially inclusive and educationally sustainable pedagogical approach for resource-constrained Higher Education Systems. Collaborative learning enhances students' analytical skills during their first year of studying accounting; therefore, it supports both long-term academic achievement, graduate employment opportunities, and work-readiness. The latter will ultimately contribute to sustaining the development of the accounting profession in South Africa. Furthermore, this type of learning promotes educational resilience because it increases student participation/engagement and decreases dropout rates without increasing institutional resources. The results indicated that the students who participated in collaborative learning had better analytical reasoning, increased self-confidence in resolving difficult financial accounting problems, and an increase in motivation throughout their transition to studying at the University level. The key elements of successful collaborative learning included: structured group discussion, peer-teaching, and collaborative problem-solving activities. Therefore, this study concluded that integrating collaborative learning in First Year Financial Accounting courses will improve students' analytical skills while providing social and educational sustainable methods of teaching and learning. Recommendations were provided for educators and curriculum developers interested in implementing collaborative learning in South African Post-Secondary Institutions.

abstract: Sustainable investing has moved environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria toward the center of cross-border capital decisions, yet the country-level evidence on whether these criteria attract foreign direct investment (FDI) rests almost entirely on static models and rarely accounts for the quality of a country’s accounting and reporting environment. This study estimates a dynamic model of FDI for 265 economies observed from 2006 to 2020, combining the three ESG pillars with four accounting and tax variables: mandatory adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), the strength of auditing standards, the extent of business disclosure, and the corporate tax burden. A fixed-effects estimator and a two-step system generalized method of moments (GMM) estimator address persistence and the reverse causality between FDI and national conditions, and a panel smooth transition regression tests whether the relationship is nonlinear. Accounting transparency attracts FDI: audit quality and disclosure carry large positive and significant coefficients under fixed effects and across income groups, while the aggregate governance index enters negatively. The corporate tax burden deters FDI with no evidence of an optimal-tax turning point. The relationship is nonlinear in governance rather than income: a panel smooth transition regression locates a governance threshold near 0.97 on the standardized scale, above which the negative association between IFRS and FDI disappears and the effects of disclosure and sustainability reporting strengthen. The results reframe the ESG–FDI question around the reporting and assurance environment through which investors read a country’s ESG credentials, and around the governance quality that makes that environment credible.

abstract: Whether a monetary anchor independent of discretionary issuance can remain stable at the macro level is the central open problem identified by the first paper of this program (Cheng and Cheng, 2026d). The present paper takes up that problem under the program’s normative premises and develops a conditional reconstruction of inflation and macrostability. We first specify the complete life cycle of the currency: issuance and extinction are mirror images of the creation and consumption of value. Consumption events trigger the cancellation of the corresponding money at the platform clearing node; durable value is extinguished on an amortization schedule that tracks physical depreciation; money issued against non-rival knowledge persists. The money stock thereby corresponds to the surviving value stock at every instant, M(t) ≡ k_s·V(t). On this basis we identify five mechanisms through which inflation is structurally precluded rather than suppressed — temporal synchrony, the quantity identity, channel excision, expectation self-stabilization, and the separation of relative prices from the price level — and we state the structural price-stability proposition with its scope made explicit: the accounting unit, the money price of a unit of negentropic value, satisfies P(t) ≡ k_s as a matter of accounting construction, while the consumer price level experienced by households is governed by the dual-price band analyzed in Section 4.7. Inflation is then rediagnosed as the relative deviation produced by four identifiable integrity failures: accounting falsification, consensus distortion, issuance corruption, and extinction failure. The zero-inflation condition, the monotonic structure of consensus distortion, and the existence of a buffering bound for the stability coefficient k_s are stated as propositions, together with a viability condition for the metabolism backstop, a composition bound on experienced inflation, an optimal buffering rule under stochastic shocks, and a tipping condition for the transition window in which the new unit coexists with legacy money. The framework’s falsifiable content is discharged computationally: five of the six pre-registered hypotheses are executed in an agent-based stress test (Appendices C and D), yielding three confirmations, one strong confirmation of the extinction layer’s necessity, and one partial falsification with a repair whose scope correction has been folded back into the main text. The sixth hypothesis — a real-world panel test of whether measurement and consensus integrity predict subsequent inflation volatility — cannot run in a model that implements the theory’s own equations; it is therefore specified as a complete pre-analysis plan with named data sources, identification strategy, and decision rules (Appendix E), executed at the pre-registered baseline depth (Appendix F), where the decision rules return not confirmed — correct signs, economically large point estimates, insufficient precision — and complemented by a long-window execution over 2003–2022 (Appendix H), which finds a strong and robust between-economy association but no statistically identified within-economy effect. The hypothesis therefore enters the literature as a constitutional-level regularity, not a short-run causal claim, with its falsification conditions and verdict discipline intact. All simulation parameters are labeled by provenance, and replication materials are specified in the appendices. The computational results are internal consistency demonstrations within the model’s own ontology, not external validation; the framework is deliberately single-system, with exchange-rate and cross-border spillovers deferred to a future international extension, and the institutional guardianship of the four integrity conditions treated in the companion governance paper (Cheng and Cheng, 2026c).

abstract: A relative source contribution factor is applied when deriving noncancer health-based guidance values for drinking water contaminants. The present work aimed at assessing the adequacy of the 20% default value often attributed to this factor while accounting for concomitant inhalation exposure to the reference concentration (RfC). Steady-state toxicokinetic equations were applied to calculate constant blood concentration (Cblood<sub>ss</sub>) in adults and 1-3-year-old children for 12 volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Three exposure scenarios were considered for each compound, namely, (1) ingestion of the reference dose (RfD) alone; (2) inhalation of the RfC alone; and (3) ingestion of 20% of the RfD combined with inhalation of the RfC. Using Monte Carlo simulations, probabilistic ratios of Cblood<sub>ss</sub> were computed for Scenario 3 over Scenario 1. Ratios >1, demonstrating an exceedance of the RfD-equivalent Cblood<sub>ss</sub> by Scenario 3, are obtained at mean and 97.5<sup>th</sup> percentile value for eight of the chosen VOCs in adults, with range of 0.3-29 at the mean and of 0.32-52 at the 97.5<sup>th</sup> percentile. Nine VOCs exhibited such exceedance in children (ranges: 0.34-36 at the mean; 0.38-57 at the 97.5<sup>th</sup> percentile). For eight VOCs, ratios >1 were mainly explained by high RfC-related intake as compared to RfD-related intake. Concluding, steady-state toxicokinetic modeling was successfully used to illustrate the importance of other media's guidance levels-related exposures, in the present case the RfC, to evaluate the magnitude of the relative source contribution factor required when determining health-based guidance values for chemicals in drinking water.

abstract: Solar water splitting should be evaluated by its oxygen-side products as well as hydrogen evolution. GaN/InGaN systems provide established examples of overall water splitting, while H<sub>2</sub>/H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> coproduction, accompanied by O<sub>2</sub> formation, has been reported for Pd-modified GaN nanowires in alkaline seawater. We examine how light absorption, charge transport, and local heating in GaN-derived structures affect oxygen-product formation and peroxide stability. Full-spectrum utilization is assessed through the distinct contributions of carriers and heat. This Perspective connects hydrogen production with oxygen-product identification, oxygen-source tracing, and peroxide stability. Product balances and measurements of carrier and thermal effects provide a basis for evaluating GaN-derived material design.

abstract: Purpose: This article aims to explore the impact of green accounting on economic prosperity and economic downturn in 82 countries over the period from 2002 to 2020. At the same time, it examines the extent of the effects of excessive expansion and severe contraction of green accounting across different phases of the economic cycle. Design/methodology/approach: The study applies a Bayesian Logistic regression model to provide a more comprehensive and deeper understanding of the impact of green accounting on phases of economic fluctuations. Findings: The results indicate that green accounting has a positive effect on economic prosperity, with estimated coefficients ranging from 0.0042 to 0.0049, together with posterior probabilities from 99.92% to 99.99%. In addition, both the expansion and the contraction of green accounting contribute to an increase in economic prosperity, although these effects are only short term. For periods of economic downturn, green accounting shows a mitigating effect, with coefficients ranging from − 0.0014 to -0.0017 and posterior probabilities from 97.78% to 99.99%. However, excessive expansion or severe contraction of green accounting worsens economic downturn, indicating the need to implement green accounting in a balanced and well targeted manner. Originality/value: This study contributes by developing a composite measurement framework for green accounting and by examining the asymmetric effects of excessive expansion and severe contraction of green accounting on the economic cycle. abstract:
Background

Heterogeneity in mosquito exposure at a fine spatial scale is well documented but often neglected in mathematical models of arbovirus transmission, particularly for real-time forecasting. We aimed to assess whether accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure improves the ability of transmission models to reproduce past chikungunya outbreaks and to forecast an ongoing outbreak in real time.

Methods

We extended an existing transmission model, originally developed to forecast dengue outbreaks in Reunion Island and incorporating seasonality, to include heterogeneity in mosquito exposure. We compared this model to versions assuming homogeneous exposure, evaluating their ability to reproduce the 2005-06 Reunion Island outbreak and the 2023 Paraguay Metropolitana subregion outbreak. We then used the heterogeneity model to forecast the 2025 Reunion Island outbreak in real time.

Findings

Accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure at a fine spatial scale was crucial to accurately reproduce Reunion Island's 2005-06 outbreak. Homogeneity models either overestimated final seroprevalence (80% vs 38% observed) or required a reduction of approximately 50% in the basic reproduction number following interventions, which is implausible. The heterogeneity level estimated from this outbreak transferred successfully to the Metropolitana outbreak, accurately forecasting epidemic trajectory and final seroprevalence (∼40% vs ∼75% for the homogeneity model). Under the same assumption, the heterogeneity model successfully forecasted the peak of the 2025 Reunion Island outbreak (∼400 emergency room visits per week) and timing (April), nearly two months ahead. A post-outbreak serosurvey indicated that the heterogeneity model underestimated final seroprevalence (46·1% vs 61·6% observed), whereas the homogeneity model overestimated final seroprevalence (78·5%), suggesting that heterogeneity in 2025 might have been lower than that in 2005-06.

Interpretation

These results highlight how incorporating heterogeneity in mosquito exposure can improve chikungunya outbreaks forecasting. Our approach showed strong predictive performance in settings with climatic seasonality and holds promise for forecasting future chikungunya and other arbovirus outbreaks.

abstract: Pain and functional limitation in knee osteoarthritis are not always proportional to radiographic severity. This cross-sectional study examined whether worry and rumination were associated with pain and functional impairment after accounting for Kellgren-Lawrence (K-L) severity. We included 156 consecutive patients with K-L grade 1 to 4 knee osteoarthritis recruited from an orthopedics outpatient clinic between February and April 2026. In bilateral cases, the predominantly symptomatic knee was used for K-L grading and scale-based symptom assessment. Pain intensity was assessed with the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and symptom burden and functional limitation were evaluated using the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC). Worry and rumination were measured with the Penn State Worry Questionnaire and Ruminative Thought Style Questionnaire, respectively. Associations were examined using Spearman correlations and multivariable linear regression for total WOMAC and VAS scores, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, K-L grade, worry, and rumination. VAS, WOMAC stiffness, physical function, and total scores differed significantly across K-L grades, whereas WOMAC pain did not; worry and rumination did not differ across radiographic severity groups. After false discovery rate correction, rumination showed the strongest correlations with WOMAC and VAS outcomes. In multivariable analyses, K-L grade and rumination were independently associated with total WOMAC (adjusted R2 = 0.379; K-L: B = 7.066, β = 0.374, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.164-9.969, P < .001; rumination: B = 0.372, β = 0.566, 95% CI: 0.255-0.489, P < .001) and VAS (adjusted R2 = 0.220; K-L: B = 0.793, β = 0.354, 95% CI: 0.407-1.179, P < .001; rumination: B = 0.036, β = 0.463, 95% CI: 0.021-0.052, P < .001). In patients with knee osteoarthritis, symptom severity appears to reflect both structural disease burden and cognitive-emotional factors. Rumination was independently associated with pain and functional limitation beyond radiographic severity, supporting a biopsychosocial approach to clinical assessment.

abstract: Objective Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a major public health concern with serious implications for adolescents' mental health. Using longitudinal data, this study examined the mechanisms linking school sports atmosphere (SSA) to NSSI among adolescents, focusing on the chain-mediating role of school connectedness (SC) and school bullying victimization (SBV). Methods The School Sports Atmosphere Scale, School Connectedness Scale, Olweus Bully/Victim Questionnaire, and Adolescent Non-suicidal Self-injury Assessment Questionnaire were administered to 987 adolescents in a two-wave longitudinal study spanning six months. The data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 26.0. Results 1. All four study variables were significantly correlated; 2. Cross-lagged analysis showed that SSA at Time 1 (T1) negatively predicted NSSI at Time 2 (T2) (β = -0.229, p < 0.01), indicating that higher SSA at T1 was associated with lower levels of NSSI six months later; 3. Mediation analysis identified three significant indirect effects: T1 SSA → T1 SC → T2 NSSI (indirect effect = -0.170, 95% CI [-0.308, -0.042]), accounting for 28% of the total effect; T1 SSA → T2 SBV → T2 NSSI (indirect effect = -0.125, 95% CI [-0.262, -0.043]), accounting for 21%; and T1 SSA → T1 SC → T2 SBV → T2 NSSI (indirect effect = -0.141, 95% CI [-0.271, -0.072]), accounting for 23%. Conclusion This study provides preliminary longitudinal evidence regarding the mechanisms linking SSA to NSSI among adolescents. SSA prospectively predicted NSSI through the separate mediating pathways of SC and SBV and the chain-mediating pathway linking SC to SBV. These findings may inform efforts to prevent and intervene in adolescent NSSI and support the development of more targeted intervention strategies.

abstract: Combustion CO2 emissions are commonly estimated by multiplying fuel consumption by the corresponding emission factors. However, national inventories may apply domestic factors to imported fuels, overlooking differences in fuel properties across extraction origins and creating discrepancies in emission estimates. Here, we trace fossil fuels to their countries of extraction and assign emission factors specific to the extraction country and fuel type. Using 2020 data for 150 countries and regions, we compare this origin-traced estimate with a nonorigin-traced control using the same energy-consumption data but combustion-country emission factors. Globally, the control estimate is 339.2 Mt of CO2 lower than the origin-traced estimate, equivalent to 1.0% of the origin-traced total, with coal accounting for 89.9% of the discrepancy. Although crude oil had the largest energy-based trade volume among primary fuels, oil-related fuels contributed less because their emission factors varied less across countries, particularly for refined petroleum products. Such discrepancies can be particularly consequential for highly import-dependent countries. For example, the national-level discrepancy exceeds 4% in India, which is a major fossil-fuel importer. Our origin-tracing approach can improve the accuracy of combustion CO2 estimates by assigning emission factors that better reflect the fuels actually consumed. This provides more robust emission information for assessing progress toward Nationally Determined Contributions.

abstract:
Objective

To assess the association between diagnostic delay and major organ involvement (MOI) in Behçet's syndrome (BS), accounting for time at risk and heterogeneity in disease trajectories.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective monocentric cohort study including 173 patients with BS fulfilling ISG and/or ICBD criteria and with at least 5 years of follow-up. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of MOI (ocular, neurological, gastrointestinal or vascular involvement). Diagnostic delay was defined as the time from symptom onset to diagnosis. Logistic regression and sensitivity models assessed the association between diagnostic delay and cumulative MOI, accounting for age at onset, sex and disease duration. Time-to-event analyses were performed among patients without MOI at disease onset to evaluate incident MOI during follow-up.

Results

Among 173 patients, 101 (58.4%) had at least one cumulative MOI. Timing of first MOI was available for 100 patients: 67 had MOI already present at disease onset, whereas 33 developed incident MOI during follow-up. Diagnostic delay was longer in patients with cumulative MOI than in those without MOI. In the initial logistic regression model adjusted for age at onset and sex, diagnostic delay was associated with cumulative MOI; however, this association was attenuated after accounting for disease duration. Time-to-event analysis among patients without MOI at disease onset did not show a statistically significant association between diagnostic delay and incident MOI.

Conclusions

Diagnostic delay was associated with cumulative MOI in BS; however, this association was attenuated after accounting for disease duration and time at risk. The findings support the existence of heterogeneous disease trajectories, including early severe disease, incident MOI during follow-up and absence of MOI over the observed period. These results should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective longitudinal studies.

abstract: Eating less than the body needs underlies most weight-loss plans, but a sustained calorie deficit also costs lean muscle, thins hair, lowers mood and leaves people hungry. Diet-planning software rarely models these effects and usually optimises the calorie count alone. We built a diet planner that treats them as goals in their own right. From a person's sex, age, height, weight and activity level the system sets personal energy and nutrient targets, then uses an evolutionary algorithm to search 2,307 foods from the USDA database for a day of eating that supports mood, hair, muscle and fullness while limiting unhealthy nutrients and holding the energy target. Each goal is scored only from nutrients whose supporting evidence survived an audit, which removed fourteen candidate terms. For an active 27-year-old man on an 801 kcal daily deficit, the recommended plan met 101% of an activity-scaled protein target, where Mediterranean, DASH and MIND plans at the same energy reached 71 to 84%, and its micronutrient adequacy (95.4%) was higher than that of all 2,000 random feasible diets tested. All eight test profiles met their protein targets. A nutrition counsellor judged the plans nutritionally sound but often impractical to serve as written.

abstract: Religious tourism constitutes a vital component of West Bengal’s cultural ethos and local economic landscape. Major pilgrimage centers—including the Dakshineswar Kali Temple, Kalighat Kali Temple, Tarapith Temple, Taraknath Temple at Tarakeswar, and ISKCON Mayapur—draw millions of devotees annually, sustaining local micro-enterprises, transportation networks, and hospitality services. However, intensive and highly seasonal visitor inflows generate severe ecological pressure, manifesting as increased greenhouse gas emissions, solid waste accumulation, water resource depletion, and strain on municipal drainage systems. This paper presents an integrated methodological and conceptual research framework evaluating the ecological footprint of these popular temples using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), environmental resource accounting, and the Contingent Valuation Method (CVM). The methodology combines spatial land-use analysis via Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, transport-related carbon accounting, site-level material flow audits, and willingness-to-pay (WTP) econometric modeling. GIS multi-criteria overlay techniques delineate spatial environmental vulnerability zones surrounding temple complexes, while econometric models examine the socioeconomic and attitudinal drivers of visitors' financial commitment to environmental conservation. By connecting spatial exposure, resource demand, and public willingness to pay, this research framework provides an empirical foundation for low-carbon pilgrimage transport, sustainable waste management, and community-supported environmental governance.

abstract: The purpose of the study is to summarize and to analyze results of national and foreign studies concerning incorporation of sociological studies in occupational medicine. The analysis of databases of PubMed, eLibrary, Cohrane Library, MEDLINE was carried out according keywords: sociology of occupational medicine, social factors, occupational risk, occupational diseases, occupational pathology, the occupational risk management system. The sampling for analysis included 257 sources. The publications review permitted to substantiate incorporation of sociological studies on medicine, health, traumatism, morbidity, labor, employment, professions and risk as basis for new problem field in occupational medicine. This area can be denoted as the sociology of occupational medicine and in considerable extent has applied character. The consideration of social problems is directly related to development of general scientific knowledge and formation of concept of risk, including in medicine. The practical application of results of theoretical methodological and applied sociological studies can contribute to critical comprehension of key factors of management of occupational risks, improvement of quality of life of workers and preservation of labor longevity.

abstract: Artistic entrepreneurship is a rapidly changing field due to the growing dominance of social media. Digital technologies have opened up new avenues for artists to produce, market, and monetize their creative work, and have also remediated the social mechanisms, identities, and structures through which artistic value is created and recognised. Research on social media has so far focused on entrepreneurial, marketing and technological aspects, particularly platform adoption, digital marketing and economic performance. As a result, little attention has been given to understanding artrepreneurship as a socially constructed activity, influenced by platform infrastructures, algorithmic governance, digital labour, identity performance and networked social relationships. This Perspective calls for a reorientation from viewing social media as a communication medium toward understanding platforms as digitally mediated institutional environments that shape artistic production, visibility, legitimacy, and entrepreneurial opportunity. This article proposes a conceptual framework that integrates insights from digital sociology, platform studies, social capital theory, and Goffman's dramaturgical perspective to understand contemporary artistic entrepreneurship: Digital Sociology of Artrepreneurship (DSA). DSA conceptualises artrepreneurship as a dynamic process in which individual agency interacts with platform-mediated social structures, with artistic and entrepreneurial outcomes shaped by visibility, identity performance, networked relations and strategic engagements within digitally mediated ecosystems. A research agenda for the future and theoretical implications for sociology, cultural studies, entrepreneurship, and research on a digital society are presented in the conclusion.

abstract: Revolutions are an extremely important topic in sociology. At the same time, the approaches and theoretical bases for analyzing revolutions change with each new generation of revolution researchers, and accordingly, the assessments of revolutions in terms of their impact on the course of the historical process and in other aspects change, as well as the assessments of certain processes and theories. The causes of this lie both in the very variability of historical events under the influence of the development of society, technology, and the interconnectedness of the World System. Important causes lie also in the fact that each generation of revolutionary theorists corresponds to "their own revolutions," whose character is both similar and dissimilar to the previous revolutionary storms. But in addition to this, a very important reason for the change of paradigms in assessing and analyzing revolutions is the general course of the development of sociology, the change in its approaches and means of analysis. Almost every theory of revolution is in one way or another based on some major sociological trends and theories or on theories of social psychology, political sociology, and other social sciences related to sociology. However, in analyzing the evolution of views on revolutions, little attention has been paid to this side. The task of this article is to show, as far as possible, the deep connection between the development and change of revolutionary theories with the general development of sociology and important sociological theories that are associated with certain periods of sociological history; to find a correlation between the development of revolutionary theories and sociology as a whole, both conceptually and in terms of the most important stages in the development of both social scientific trends. We would like to show that there is a rather obvious correlation between the stages (epochs) of sociology's development and the change of generations of revolutionary researchers, as well as a correlation in the chronology of the change of the most important stages of sociology's history/development and the change of generations of revolutionary researchers and theories of revolution. In addition to the main text, the article includes three online appendices.

abstract: This article develops the concept of temporal structuration to explain how actors engage temporal norms as social structures. Based on 64 life story interviews in Shenzhen and analysed through constructivist grounded theory, it examines reproductive timing in urban China, where marriage and childbearing are organised by a dense timetable enforced through kin relations. The analysis identifies a situated repertoire of four types of strategy: accommodation, transformation, redirection and identity-based claims, which participants combined and redeployed as relationships, pressures and available resources changed. The strategies act upon the norm's enforcement, justification, operating conditions and applicability, respectively, while drawing on the categories and relationships that sustain it. Postponement thus emerges as a relational accomplishment, maintained through practical, justificatory, identity and emotion work. Temporal structuration thus captures the recursive process through which actors secure room for alternative timing while reproducing-and potentially, through collective accumulation, altering-the norm's authority and operation. This article therefore extends the temporal dimension of structure and agency, advances the empirical understanding of temporal agency, and enriches the processual understanding of temporal experience.

abstract: Creative entrepreneurship increasingly combines creative production with entrepreneurial, communicative, and platform-mediated work. Existing scholarship has generated important insights into opportunity recognition, innovation, value creation, and creative labor, but these perspectives often examine entrepreneurial activity, social relations, cultural recognition, and platform governance as analytically separate processes. This Perspective develops the Sociological Ecology of Creative Entrepreneurship (SECE), a conceptual framework that positions creative entrepreneurship as socially embedded work within platform society. Drawing on economic sociology, sociology of work, labor process theory, digital sociology, and platform studies, SECE integrates five analytically distinct but relationally connected dimensions: identity construction, relational capital, platform governance, cultural legitimacy, and institutional embeddedness. The framework is presented as a relational and multilevel heuristic rather than a tested causal model. It proposes that creative entrepreneurial practice emerges through interactions among workers, audiences, collaborators, platforms, cultural fields, and institutions. The Perspective further considers how these relations are shaped by power, inequality, and human-AI interaction and identifies directions for empirical research into platform-mediated creative work, occupational sustainability, and changing forms of employment.

abstract: Notions of good or bad luck sit uncomfortably in contemporary medical practice defined by efforts to control life through biomedical knowledge and skilled expertise. Yet, talk about luck is common in healthcare to explain medical courses of action. Framing medical results as fortunate or unfortunate bridges the gap between predicted probabilities and variation in individual cases without undermining scientific neutrality. Luck mediates between the rational ideal of biomedical determinism that does not easily account for variable health outcomes and the magical invocation of faith or fate that denotes a moral judgement. Drawing from ethnographic studies of heart transplantation and fertility medicine, we find that luck is employed as an anticipatory frame to guide decision-making in medicine and as a retroactive frame to justify unlikely outcomes. Invoking luck primes patients for the possibility of a favourable outcome and inserts a positive bias in medical care. The analysis underlines how luck frames in healthcare can shift attention away from structural reasons for disparate outcomes, attempt to absolve healthcare providers of blame from medical errors and promote continuing treatment. These findings indicate that focusing on when healthcare providers and patients invoke luck reveals the scope and limits of medical power and control.

abstract: Informal donor conception (IDC) has an ambiguous status under UK law. Whilst not illegal, it is discouraged by regulators and only partially recognised in attributions of legal parenthood. In this paper, we analyse IDC as a lens to explore the politics of reproductive signification. We use this term to refer to the power dynamics at play in deciding the meaning of reproductive processes in people's everyday lives. Drawing on interviews with 19 donors and 30 (intended) parents via IDC, we explore how they manage the relational significance of conception, gestation and care in the context of a legal regime which is often at odds with their intentions. Building on theories of legal consciousness and stratified reproduction, we demonstrate how the politics of reproductive signification encompass not only cis/heteronormative legislation but also the ways in which inequalities, relating to economic resources, racialised and classed parenting ideals and relationship status, shape possibilities to work with the law and resist its relational authority via practices of de-animation or embrace legal ambiguity. Our analysis has implications for understanding how people negotiate the meaning of reproduction, particularly in the context of legal marginalisation.

abstract: Since the 1990s, marked by Health's inaugural issue and the publication of Boltanski and Thévenot's De la justification, the Sociology of Health and Medicine has been shaped by traditions rooted in Critical Sociology, particularly Foucauldian, Marxist, and Bourdieusian paradigms. These frameworks have offered incisive critiques of power, biopolitics, medicalization, and neoliberal reframing of health responsibility. Concurrently, another sociological movement emerged through the development of French Pragmatic Sociology, or the "sociology of critical capacity." By foregrounding actors' justifications, plural conceptions of worth, and regimes of engagement, it reorients the analysis from structural domination to situated critique, one that is attuned to the complexity, uncertainty, and ambivalence of health-related action. It enables a relational, context-sensitive approach to the lived experiences of patients and professionals as they engage with institutional arrangements and enact critique within situated action. Drawing on a non-exhaustive, interpretive review of empirical studies engaging with Pragmatic Sociology, particularly in healthcare controversies, clinical decision-making, patient-professional interactions, and health innovation, this article shows how this perspective fosters nuanced understandings of normativity, critique, and coordination in health practices. It traces this theoretical realignment and argues that Pragmatic Sociology offers a compelling, flexible, and still underutilized epistemological and methodological framework for health research, sustaining and extending critique through an empirically grounded analysis.

abstract: This paper examines how distance impacts the network of connections across social movement organisations. Much of the social movements research on scale and spatiality has focused on micro (the immediate vicinity in protest events) and macro levels (local-global connections), with limited attention paid to the role played by distance in shaping networks across a single country context. To examine this phenomenon, we analyse Extinction Rebellion Australia: an environmental social movement organisation that diffused from the densely populated and spatially compact UK to Australia, with its geographically concentrated populations separated by large distances. Building on Davis' power of distance framework, this paper introduces the power of inter-chapter distance: a framework wherein physical, institutional, cultural, and class-based distances shape network connections within social movements. Our network analysis revealed four network archetypes: a bridge-rich core spans the eastern coast from Melbourne to Brisbane, while affinity-clustered, chapter-centred, and bifurcated systems are found elsewhere in the country. A thematic analysis then draws on rich qualitative data to discuss how inter-chapter distances impact the character of mobilisation in Extinction Rebellion Australia.

abstract: With recent changes to the health information landscape, understanding how sources of health information are associated with preventive health behaviors (PHBs) remains an important area for research. In particular, understanding where structurally marginalized populations like Hispanic immigrants receive trusted health information- and how this information is associated with PHBs-is critical, given their more limited access to formal information sources. Further, how gender patterns the association between trust in information sources and PHBs is often overlooked in research on structurally marginalized groups. In this study, we examine how Hispanic immigrants' trusted sources of information are associated with PHBs protecting against COVID-19, focusing on how this association varies by gender. We leverage data from the VidaSana Study, a survey of Hispanic immigrants in Indiana, and its extension, the Hispanic COVID-19 Rapid Response Study. We first identify characteristics associated with trusting sources on COVID-19 before predicting the number of PHBs as a function of trusted information sources and gender. Results indicate that participants who trust the radio as a source of information about COVID-19 are more likely to engage in PHBs. However, interaction models show that men who do not trust radio or TV about COVID-19 are driving this association, as they are less likely to engage in PHBs. We suggest that traditional health communications sources focus on fostering trust among Hispanic men as a way to disseminate accurate and timely information about health concerns.

abstract: This article has three goals. The first is to explain the contributions of the Program for Research on Black Americans (PRBA) to the field of sociology. The second is to provide a review of the scope of research conducted by PRBA scholars. This review covers research on Black families, marriage and romantic relationships, racial socialization, interpersonal violence, negative interactions, religious participation and spirituality, religion and mental health, social support, social isolation, mental and physical health, racism and discrimination, colorism, and Black politics. It also covers research on African American and Black Caribbean adolescents, adults, and older adults. The third goal of the article is a bibliometric analysis of National Survey of American Life (NSAL)-based publications including citation analysis, analysis of which journals have published the most NSAL-based articles, and authorship network analysis. The article ends with a brief discussion of our most recent data collection and a conclusion. The article shows that the PRBA, through its research, mentoring, and longevity, has met the criteria of Wright and Thomas's principles of Black sociology.

abstract: Knowledge on the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis reactivity to acute psychosocial stress remains limited. The current study evaluated whether testosterone, progesterone, and estradiol increase in response to the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST), and whether these responses are attenuated in panic disorder (PD) patients compared to healthy controls (HC), given the reported hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis hyporesponsiveness in PD. Two sex- and age-matched groups (n = 30 HC, n = 30 PD; n = 19 women and n = 11 men per group) underwent the TSST. Serum gonadal steroids were measured 15 min pre- and 1, 10, and 20 min post-TSST. Mixed models revealed significant post-TSST increases in testosterone (F(3, 174) = 5.43, p = .001) and progesterone (F(3, 168) = 5.39, p = .002), but not in estradiol (F(3, 169) = 2.52, p = .06). PD patients displayed higher estradiol levels than HCs (F(1, 56) = 10.11, p = .002). Men showed higher testosterone (F(1, 57) = 675.89, p < .001) and lower progesterone (F(1, 56) = 5.38, p = .024) than women. Exploratory analyses suggested distinct temporal patterns across groups for all three gonadal steroids. These findings indicate a potential role of gonadal steroids in psychosocial stress regulation and highlight its relevance as an understudied mechanism in panic disorder. Potential factors masking main effects and interactions such as interindividual variability and sex imbalances are discussed. Future studies including larger, more sex-balanced samples are needed to clarify these patterns.

abstract: Youth exposure to violence and crime is often measured through survey data or reports from Child Protective Services, which do not capture the full extent of the problem. In this article, we used administrative data from police incident reports to examine patterns of youth exposure, as victims and witnesses, to crime and violence by youth demographic characteristics (age, race, and gender), location of exposure, and neighborhood social vulnerability. We find roughly the same raw number of incidents by race, though Black youth make up under 15% of the population within the study area. Looking at the data spatially, neighborhood social vulnerability is associated with higher incidents and multiple locations per youth. The results indicate that demographic and neighborhood factors impact youth exposure to incidents.

abstract: This article examines the representation of community within restorative justice (RJ) in the French film All Your Faces (Je verrai toujours vos visages, 2023), addressing central debates within RJ scholarship concerning the meaning, place, and function of community in restorative processes. By analysing the film's verbal and visual dimensions, the article examines how community is represented and enacted through relationships, interactions, spatial arrangements, and restorative practices. The analysis identifies three forms of community: prison as a space in which multiple communities intersect; the participatory community that emerges within the restorative circle; and communities of care that support victims and offenders throughout the restorative process. Across these dimensions, All Your Faces portrays community as an evolving social process rather than a fixed category of participants. Community is progressively produced through ritualized interaction, storytelling, humor, collective vulnerability, recognition, and practices of care. These findings shift attention from who constitutes the community in RJ to how community is enacted through restorative practices and relationships. The article contributes to interdisciplinary scholarships at the intersection of sociology, law, criminology, and victimology by conceptualizing community as a relational and institutional accomplishment. It also demonstrates the value of film as a site for examining how restorative justice practices and values are culturally imagined, interpreted, and communicated to wider publics.

abstract:
Purpose

This study aimed to assess the perceived usefulness of the sociology course among undergraduate Allied Health Sciences (AHS) students in Chennai, India.

Methods

A cross-sectional study was conducted among 240 undergraduate AHS students who were in their third and fourth years at a medical college and hospital in Chennai. The Perceived Usefulness of Sociology Course (PUSC) scale was developed and validated by the investigator and administered using Google Form. In addition, a 10-point numerical rating scale was used to assess the overall satisfaction with the sociology course.

Results

Among the 240 students, 62% were female students and 54% were studying in fourth-year. The mean score for the PUSC was 57.49 ± 9.15 and ranged from 15 to 75. Overall, 62% of the students had a high level of perceived usefulness of the sociology course. No significant differences were observed in gender and year of study. One hundred and twenty-three (51%) students rated their satisfaction with the course as high, highlighting its perceived effectiveness in meeting learning objectives in the Allied Health Sciences curriculum.

Conclusions

The study showed that undergraduate AHS students had a positive perception of the sociology course, recognising its value. They valued its role in understanding the applied social determinants of health and improving patient interactions.

abstract: Contemporary Chinese younger adults face a structural contradiction between the state-promoted biopolitics of 'Healthy China 2030' and accelerated work and study regimes. This study examines how young people enact and coordinate multiple bodily realities through everyday wellness practices and seek to maintain a workable body under these competing demands. Grounded in Annemarie Mol's theory of enactment, a reflexive thematic analysis of netnographic observations and 28 semi-structured interviews identifies four representative embodied strategies: punk wellness, modern medical wellness, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) wellness, and hybrid wellness. These strategies reflect different modes and degrees of bodily coordination, ranging from low-integration bricolage to coordination within a dominant bodily reality and, finally, reflexive meta-coordination across modern medical and TCM-derived practices. The study introduces 'reflexive fluency' to capture hybrid wellness practitioners' embodied capacity to navigate heterogeneous health repertoires and bodily realities. As a form of embodied cultural capital, this fluency reveals emerging patterns of health stratification. By shifting the focus of 'coordination' from medical institutions to individuals, the study shows how mundane bodily practices become a means of managing structural constraints. These findings contribute to debates on biopolitics, embodiment, and health stratification in post-reform China.

abstract: Recorded diagnoses of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism in adults have risen sharply across high-income health systems, and demand for assessment has risen faster still, while the best available population estimates of prevalence appear to have moved comparatively little. This paper treats that divergence as an analytic problem. We argue that adult neurodevelopmental diagnosis has undergone a threefold transformation: it has become demand-led and co-produced rather than professionally imposed, identity-conferring rather than merely descriptive, and self-reinforcing rather than static. The result is a diagnostic culture efficient at conferring diagnoses but weak, unsystematic and largely untheorised in reconsidering them. Drawing on the sociology of diagnosis, labelling theory, Ian Hacking's account of interactive kinds and discourse-analytic studies of diagnostic contestation, we examine how demand-led medicalisation, the reframing of diagnosis as valued identity and the expansive use of the camouflaging construct can impede revision in practice. Against this background we develop the concept of diagnostic revisability: the capacity of a diagnostic culture to reconsider a diagnostic judgement, in either direction, in the light of change in the person or in the evidence. We distinguish correction of an insecure original judgement, revision in response to change, supersession and reversal of a non-diagnosis, and argue that revisability is an intrinsic property of diagnosis understood as defeasible inference. Precedents exist in medication review and deprescribing and in diagnostic de-labelling elsewhere in medicine. The case is stronger for ADHD, where symptoms and diagnostic status fluctuate and diagnosis is linked to prescribing, than for autism, where it rests principally on the security of the original assessment. Recent Swedish proposals for de-diagnosis services make revisability visible as an object of policy, but the conceptual case does not itself entail support for any service model. Diagnostic revision may correct error; it may also threaten identity, access to support and self-understanding, fall unequally on particular groups, or become a mechanism for rationing. If revisability is translated into practice, it must therefore satisfy stringent ethical and institutional safeguards, including an explicit equity criterion. The design requirements presented are minimum conditions for responsible revision and criteria for when it should not proceed.

abstract: Tri-Agency-funded researchers in Canada will soon be required, with few exceptions, to deposit data and make them available, including for possible reuse by others. These new requirements will upend the data management practices of sociologists in Canada, especially qualitative researchers. In this essay, I review the emerging Tri-Agency requirements and explore current data management practices of sociologists in Canada through a scan of CRS articles. I situate data deposit and availability in the broader context of open science, and then explore debates-epistemological and ethical-among qualitative researchers outside of Canada where data deposit mandates are already in place. I briefly raise issues that require the attention of (especially qualitative) sociologists in Canada relating to community-based research and to data access. I conclude the essay by recommending sociologists-especially qualitative sociologists-assess our readiness for the new data regime.

abstract: This paper examines the interpretation and use of The Invisible Religion in Japanese sociology of religion, its impact, and the background to that impact. Luckmann’s work was introduced in discussions of “secularization” through the reception in Japan of sociological theories developed in Europe and the United States. It was later cited as a theoretical framework for “privatization,” especially in analyses of the emergence of spirituality. During the initial stage of its reception, attention was paid to Luckmann’s functional conception of religion as an anthropological condition. Subsequently, however, his work came to be treated primarily as one perspective among others on secularization or privatization. Moreover, although his functional definition derives from phenomenology and his work was later placed under the rubric of “phenomenological sociology,” the question of what made this perspective phenomenological, or what significance it derived from phenomenology, was not raised. Despite limited examination of the distinctiveness of his theory, Luckmann’s argument continued to be cited because theories of secularization and privatization had become familiar and widely shared. As a result, the radical significance of this definition became invisible—namely, its potential to identify the religious function of phenomena that appear nonreligious and thereby call into question the distinction between religion and nonreligion. This paper proposes two hypotheses regarding this process. First, privatization became commonplace, leaving little occasion to question either the concept of religion or the boundaries of what counts as religion in modern Japanese society. Second, the term “phenomenological sociology” became sufficiently established to be taken for granted.

abstract: Objectives. To examine whether the timing of family member deaths across the life course is associated with cognitive impairment and dementia in midlife to later life. Methods. Using 20 years of longitudinal data (2000-2020) from the US Health and Retirement Study and competing risks models, we examined how age at the time of a parent's, child's, or spouse's death is associated with the onset of mid-to-later-life cognitive impairment with or without dementia. Results. Among individuals who experienced family member deaths, losses occurring at younger ages were associated with higher risks of cognitive impairment than losses occurring at older ages. The association for parental and spousal death timing became statistically nonsignificant after adjustment for early-life and adult health factors, whereas associations for child death timing remained robust across model specifications. We found no evidence of racial/ethnic or gender differences in these patterns. Conclusions. Our study identifies timing of bereavement as an underrecognized determinant of cognitive aging and highlights earlier-life loss as a strategic target for prevention and intervention.
