abstract:
Background

Thalassemia is a major monogenic blood disorder, with India bearing a substantial burden. Although carrier screening is the most effective preventive strategy, inconsistent criteria, borderline HbA2 values, diverse mutations, and limited HbE detection hinder effectiveness. This study determines the prevalence of molecularly confirmed beta thalassemia trait (BTT) and HbE detected through a large-scale screening approach among young adults in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and develops a potential scalable model for university-based carrier detection.

Methods

We recruited 4886 young adults aged 18-35 years from universities in Delhi-NCR. All blood samples underwent CBC and HPLC analysis, with selected samples subjected to genetic analysis using ARMS-PCR and Sanger sequencing.

Results

The prevalence of molecularly confirmed BTT and HbE trait detected through the study screening approach was 1.6% and 0.4%, respectively. Overall, 2% showed elevated HbA2 with low MCV and MCH, while 5.1% of carriers had borderline HbA2. Five common beta thalassemia mutations accounted for 84.8% of cases. Nearly 21% of samples with HbA2 4-9% showed no mutations on genetic testing. HbA2 4-9% plus low MCV and MCH showed the highest PPV, with 92% sensitivity and 88% specificity. No significant differences in BTT distribution were observed by region, religion, or social category.

Conclusions

Large-scale screening for BTT among young adults in university-based settings may facilitate early carrier identification. HbA2 levels of 4-9% combined with low MCV and MCH appear to be an effective first-tier screening criterion, while further criteria are needed to identify and prioritize individuals with borderline HbA2 levels (3.2-3.9%) for molecular confirmation. Future studies should focus on developing and validating robust, context-appropriate population-level screening protocols for BTT in India.

abstract: The American Journal of Human Biology (AJHB), the flagship journal of the Human Biology Association, has published research on human biology, health, and disease since 1989. The goal of this study is to identify the dominant research themes published in the journal and track their evolution over this 36-year period. To achieve this goal, we adopted a mixed-methods approach that combined large language model (LLM) topic modeling, using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), with qualitative expert review. Our dataset comprised 3348 abstracts and metadata (e.g., author, year, title) published between 1989 and April 2025 retrieved from PubMed. We used BERT-based clustering as a first-pass classifier and then expert consensus to consolidate the clusters into themes. Fifteen major themes emerged. We then examined temporal changes in these 15 themes. Two themes that have and continue to dominate are Growth and Development and Body Composition. In contrast, Genetics, while common, declined in recent years. Maternal, Fetal, and Infant Health, and Demography and Reproduction, while always well-represented, increased, especially since 2010. Meanwhile, the less-prevalent themes Stress Biology, Nutrition, and Human Biology Frameworks have shown gradual growth. Overall, while a set of themes dominate the journal's corpus of scholarship, the trends we found indicate a transition toward more theory-driven analyses of health and disease and underscore the journal's responsiveness to emerging scientific paradigms and global health challenges, offering a roadmap for future scholarship.

abstract:
Background

Serum vitamin D status and vitamin D receptor (VDR) genetic variation may contribute to kidney stone disease (KSD) susceptibility, although their combined effects remain poorly understood. This study investigated the independent and combined effects of serum vitamin D status and VDR genetic variation on KSD susceptibility in a genetically homogeneous population.

Methods

A case-control study was conducted on 267 KSD patients and 296 metabolically screened controls. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured, and VDR ApaI, TaqI, and FokI polymorphisms were genotyped by PCR-RFLP. Haplotype, linkage disequilibrium, ROC, and additive gene-environment interaction analyses were performed.

Results

Individual VDR polymorphisms were not significantly associated with KSD. However, elevated serum vitamin D was strongly associated with disease risk (OR = 12.55, 95% CI: 4.70-33.54; p < 0.001). ROC analysis identified an optimal vitamin D cut-off of 35.84 ng/mL (AUC = 0.816). Haplotype analysis identified GCC as a risk haplotype (OR = 4.08, 95% CI: 2.47-6.72), whereas GCT (OR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.10-0.46) was protective. Additive interaction analyses demonstrated positive interactions between elevated serum vitamin D and the ApaI GT and FokI CC/CT genotypes, while TaqI variants showed antagonistic interactions.

Conclusion

The study highlights that VDR haplotypes and serum vitamin D-VDR genotype interactions substantially modified disease risk, suggesting that integrating biochemical and genetic markers may improve KSD risk assessment and support precision prevention strategies.

abstract:
Objective

Porous skeletal lesion (PSL) is a descriptive term for bone altered by macroscopic perforations or pits. This paper seeks to assist researchers in meaningfully interpreting PSLs by offering perspectives on the currently available imaging modalities and approaches to better evaluate these important lesions. As a macro-morphological category, PSL is diagnostically non-specific; such lesions can result from formative defects, resorptive activity, or their interplay, and may be seen in normal development, disease and related conditions.

Methods

We outline imaging modalities available for investigating PSL: macroscopic methods, microscopy (including histology), radiography (including computed tomography), and more recent clinical techniques such as magnetic resonance imaging.

Results

Each modality produced useful information about PSLs and had strengths and weaknesses.

Conclusions

Although macroscopic observation is often the most widely available, it is frequently insufficient to differentiate proximate causes and ultimate diagnostic probabilities. For a detailed understanding of tissue-level pathophysiology, the high resolution and visibility of internal features provided by micro-CT and microscopy are strong diagnostic aids, while clinical modalities (CT, radiography, MRI) offer the advantage of enabling comparisons with PSLs in contemporary populations and links to soft tissue features.

Significance

The spectrum of techniques now available offers options to all researchers. Understanding the potential and limitations is, however, critical to getting the most from any investigation.

Suggestions for future research

We advocate for more cross-sectional imaging of PSLs to better understand the etiologies and morphological distinctions of these lesions. Greater integration of clinical techniques and data offers considerable potential for better understanding deceased individuals.

abstract:
Objectives

According to the American Association of Biological Anthropologists Code of Ethics, "departments offering anthropology degrees should include and require ethical training in their curriculums." Ethics training is essential, but are Anthropology undergraduate and graduate programs incorporating ethics education as part of their core curriculum? Do Anthropology undergraduate and graduate students feel like they are receiving adequate education and training in ethics as part of their program curriculum?

Materials and methods

This study attempts to answer these questions by analyzing undergraduate degree requirements for Anthropology majors in the U.S. and by surveying U.S.-based Anthropology teaching faculty and undergraduate and graduate students. These surveys include questions about Anthropology curricula, program and course learning objectives, and student preparedness in facing ethical dilemmas post-graduation. In total, 142 individuals participated in the survey (94 students, 48 faculty members).

Results

The results of this survey indicate that some Anthropology undergraduate and graduate programs are incorporating ethics education as part of their core curriculum, but this is not true for all programs. Unfortunately, the most frequent response was that ethics education was not incorporated into the core curriculum, and students, especially graduate students, do not feel that they are receiving adequate ethics education.

Discussion

Results of this study reveal a gap between the ideal practice proposed in professional academic organizations' codes of ethics and the reality of this application, as well as a disconnect between faculty and student perceptions of the sufficiency of the ethics education being provided. Specific recommendations for filling these gaps are provided.

abstract:
Objectives

Odds of death from specific causes in infants, children, and adolescents in Alaska have not been quantified with vital records. We analyze the odds of death from 12 causes in individuals ≤ 18 years.

Methods

We fit a multinomial logistic regression model (n = 12 904 death records) controlling for Indigeneity, age, sex, and year of death to predict the odds of specific causes of death.

Results

Alaska Native individuals were most likely to die from tuberculosis and respiratory infections, while non-Alaska Native individuals were most likely to die from early infant health problems and accidents/violence. Infectious diseases and nutritional and endocrine disorders were most likely in ages 0-5, while accidents/violence, cardiovascular issues, and tuberculosis were most likely in ages 10-18.

Conclusions

Proportionate mortality and odds of death differed significantly, reflecting the different structures of Alaska Native versus non-Alaska Native populations in the 20th century and reinforcing demographic observations in the historical record.

abstract: This article introduces a semiotic-Bayesian epistemological framework for the analysis and interpretation of skeletal trauma in forensic anthropology. The model integrates Peircean semiotics with probabilistic inference to provide a structured, reproducible approach to evaluating forensic evidence under conditions of uncertainty. Bone injuries are conceptualized as signs that maintain a causal relationship with the events that produced them; their interpretation begins with abductive reasoning, through which the forensic anthropologist formulates plausible hypotheses about the origin of the observed trauma. These hypotheses are subsequently organized through the abductive-deductive-inductive (ADI) cycle and formally evaluated using likelihood ratios (LR), derived from empirical frequency data reported in the published literature, to quantify the strength of the evidence. This proposal is illustrated through three forensic cases involving cranial blunt force trauma, cervicocephalic injuries associated with interpersonal violence, and close-range gunshot wounds. In each case, the framework enabled logical quantification of evidential weight, enhancing interpretive transparency, mitigating cognitive bias and facilitating communication within judicial contexts. The methodology proposed bridges qualitative, context-driven interpretation with quantitative rigor, thereby addressing longstanding epistemological challenges aligning anthropological practice with modern legal standards of admissibility, and highlighting the important role of the LR as a logically coherent and reproducible measure of strength.

abstract: Due to their strong correlation to heredity, nonmetric dental traits are deemed useful to estimate an individual's population affinity. This case report demonstrates the use of the rASUDAS2 application for estimating a decedent's population affinity when other primary identification methods proved insufficient. Initial examinations showed that the decedent (referred to as KF230565 or Mr X) was a 42-year-old male whose death was caused by non-homicidal drowning. Due to slight deviations from the typical Western Indonesian craniofacial characteristics, his nonmetric dental traits were graded to confirm his population affinity. After grading the dental traits according to the Arizona State University Dental Anthropology System (ASUDAS), the data were entered into the rASUDAS2 software. Based on the analysis, the decedent was estimated to be of Western Eurasian (46.24%) or Southeast Asian (20.58%) affinity. This information was then passed to forensic artists and law enforcement, and a facial approximation sketch was constructed using the appropriate population-specific soft tissue thickness dataset. The sketches were then disseminated to the public to aid recognition. After receiving additional reports from the public, positive identification of the decedent was confirmed through primary identifiers. This report encourages the use of multidisciplinary methods in forensic identification, as well as further studies on dental morphology.

abstract: Stature estimation is one key component of the biological profile in forensic anthropology, yet most available regression formulae are derived from non-contemporary and non-UK reference samples. This study aimed to develop and evaluate preliminary PMCT-derived regression equations for estimating cadaveric length from long-bone measurements in a contemporary East London mortuary sample; and to compare their performance with commonly used Trotter and Gleser formulae. Whole-body PMCT scans of 100 adults from the East London Forensic Centre were analysed, comprising 50 males and 50 females aged 25-97 years. Bilateral measurements of the humerus, femur, tibia, and fibula were recorded in Horos using standard osteometric definitions. Side-averaged values were used in ordinary least squares regression models, with cadaveric length as the outcome variable. Both univariate and limited multivariate models were generated for pooled and sex-specific samples, and model performance was assessed in a number of ways such as adjusted R<sup>2</sup>, standard error of estimate, root mean square error, mean absolute error, and cross-validation. Results indicate that lower limb variables showed the strongest associations with cadaveric length. However, the high inter-predictor correlations and VIF values indicated severe multicollinearity, meaning that the most complex multivariable models should not be interpreted biologically or treated as the strongest practical option. Instead, the findings support the use of parsimonious, sex-specific equations, with wider multivariable models presented cautiously as internally fitted models only. This study provides population-relevant PMCT-derived reference equations for a small contemporary East London sample, but external validation is required before routine forensic implementation.

abstract: The evolution of human bipedalism has traditionally been reconstructed from the pelvis and lower limb, whereas the contribution of the vertebral motion segment has received far less attention. This study introduces the vertebral apophyseal ring (AR) as a novel proxy for reconstructing spinal biomechanics in fossil hominins. Several vertebrae with complete ARs from Australopithecus afarensis A.L. 288-1 were compared with vertebrae from 240 adult modern humans, a Neanderthal (Kebara), an Upper Paleolithic modern human (Ohalo II), 20 chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes), and 24 gorillas (Gorilla gorilla). Vertebral body and AR dimensions were measured from vertebrae T4-L5 (L4 in apes), and corresponding ratios were calculated. Statistical differences between modern humans and African apes were assessed using Welch's analysis of variance followed by Games-Howell post hoc tests. Relative AR size in A.L. 288-1 consistently falls within the range of chimpanzees and gorillas rather than modern humans, indicating that A. afarensis spinal motion segments differed functionally from those of modern humans. Because AR reduction is associated with enlargement of the nucleus pulposus, our findings suggest that spinal adaptations necessary for efficient load absorption, torsional flexibility, and endurance locomotion evolved later in human evolution. These results indicate that the evolution of humanlike bipedalism was a gradual and mosaic process. Although Australopithecus possessed the fundamental capacity for upright walking, it retained primitive spinal features indicative of a less optimized locomotor system. The emergence of a fully modern human gait, therefore, involved progressive reorganization of the vertebral motion segment rather than a single evolutionary transition.

abstract: "Medical desert," referring to conditions of unequal access to medical care, remains contested in its definition and measurement. Predominantly supply-focused, most studies rely on quantitative indicators and few examine how care-seekers perceive and navigate shortages, nor do they address desertification as a dynamic, policy-driven process. None, to our knowledge, compare these experiences across rural and urban settings or countries. We conducted a qualitative comparative investigation during the COVID-19 pandemic among people experiencing health and social vulnerabilities in France and Slovenia, employing the WHO Availability, Accessibility, Acceptability, and Quality (AAAQ) framework. From January to July 2021, we interviewed 156 participants in one urban (Paris-Seine-Saint-Dénis) and one rural (Vendôme territory) site in France and 214 participants in one urban (Ljubljana) and one rural (Pomurje) site in Slovenia. Thematic analysis revealed shared patterns across sites and countries. Participants in all sites reported insufficient availability of services and personnel; urban residents experienced shortages despite nominally abundant resources. Accessibility barriers extended beyond spatial distance to encompass cost, time poverty, informational gaps, digital exclusion, language barriers, and clientelism. Dissatisfaction with care quality (claims of dismissive providers, absent holistic diagnosis, eroded trust) was pervasive although invisible to standard medical desert metrics. Social vulnerabilities compounded these barriers, producing uneven experiences of desertification. These findings demonstrate that care-seeker-centered approaches can foreground processes of medical desertification that transcend the rural-urban divide. By illuminating perceived shortages that supply-side indicators miss, they suggest that desertification may reflect a broader austerity-driven erosion of public healthcare whose consequences surfaced during the pandemic.

abstract: Using gender as an analytic, I parse out how the historical gendered, classed, and racialized roots of the 12 Step Program remain present in its therapeutic model, even in global contexts beyond its original formulation. These foundations continue to shape therapeutic logics and experience within the Program, in positive and negative ways. I outline several key experiential points of friction with the 12 Step Program for women in one residential drug rehabilitation center in the United States-México border zone, demonstrating the gender of this therapeutic model's framework. Clarifying the Program's gender of care helps make sense of why so many women find this therapeutic model inadequate, without discounting the very real support 12 Step Programs have provided to both women and men around the world. Attention to these frictions with structures (in this case a therapeutic model) illuminates the implicit frameworks that organize our world and direct our attention to developing novel frameworks/institutions.

abstract: Although standard craniometrics is typically regarded as the method of choice for estimating population affinity in adults, its application to subadults has received limited attention, despite potential population-specific signals demonstrated in cranial growth patterns. This study evaluated the potential efficacy of interlandmark distances (ILDs) derived from three-dimensional (3D) cranial models obtained from Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) scans of South African black, coloured, indian and white subadults, and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to estimate population affinity. Results indicated that the combined midface and cranial base model contained the most population-specific variation, with black South Africans achieving the highest classification accuracy. The best-performing multivariate model achieved a 79.17% accuracy and a kappa of 0.67. Age-stratified models produced slightly lower classification rates, suggesting that early ontogenetic trajectories during childhood may obscure population differences. Indian South Africans were consistently misclassified across all models, likely reflecting both challenges posed by limited sample size and substantial heterogeneity and overlap with other groups. While age had a limited influence on the predictive performance, ILDs show considerable promise for subadult classification, particularly when combining measurements from the facial skeleton and cranial base. These findings indicate that population-specific craniofacial variation is detectable across subadult development and that incorporating the full developmental sample may yield more accurate classifications than age-stratified approaches.

abstract:
Objective

Advances in postmortem imaging technologies are transforming medical examiner practice, enabling the creation of large-scale digital collections of decedent data that support research across medicine, public health, forensics, bioarchaeology, paleoanthropology, demographics, and anthropology in general. Drawing on the case of the New Mexico Decedent Image Database (NMDID), this paper explores the promises and risks of virtual medicolegal collections, introduces the perspectives of next-of-kin from a pilot focus group, and confronts the gaps in existing professional and legal frameworks. Finally, this work attempts to establish a foundation for developing standards for ethical stewardship of digital remains in the modern medicolegal landscape.

Materials and methods

One pilot focus group (n = 5) was conducted in Kalamazoo, Michigan in 2022. De-identified transcripts underwent a thematic analysis by anthropologists, ethicists, and biomedical informaticians. Themes were determined when the majority of the focus group agreed or shared the same or similar statement.

Results

From the small group of five participants, seven unique themes were identified relating to the use of decedent data, from the conversations with NOK: legitimate identifiability, closure, advocacy, legitimacy of research, timing of inquiry, notification, and agency.

Discussion

Despite not obtaining saturation due to small group size, the thematic analysis still provides an important stakeholder perspective to help identify key aspects of the history and legal context of the unique ethical challenges posed by using medical examiner imaging-based collections for research purposes. Building on this foundation, we propose eight preliminary ethical guidelines that emphasize confidentiality, security, stewardship, and respect for next-of-kin.

abstract: This essay reads the overdose of "Mikey" through a death tarot card I created to honor his life. In doing so, I explore the possibility of using art to tell a broader story of community care and emotional healing. The death tarot card represents not only material death, but the potential for profound transformation. Mikey was a "street dad" to many living in an encampment whose early death is a tragedy, but whose life story reclaims community where people often see none. Can the intuitive process of creating art from ethnographic data offer medical anthropologists new analytical insights toward healing?

abstract: The estimation of the biological sex of archeological remains is crucial information in bioarcheology and forensic anthropology. In recent years, proteomics based on molecular sexual dimorphism has emerged as a preferred method, particularly because of its minimally invasive approach for extracting amelogenin X and Y proteins from tooth enamel. However, there is an increasing demand to accelerate this process and facilitate the analysis of large archeological assemblages. This study presents a novel high-throughput targeted paleoproteomics method for biological sex estimation using MALDI-CASI-FTICR mass spectrometry. This approach combines the strengths of existing methods, including ultrahigh resolution, significantly reduced processing times, targeted analysis, and scalability to large archeological sample sets. The method was initially validated on modern individuals with known sex and subsequently applied to 130 adult and juvenile individuals from medieval Great Moravia (present-day Czech Republic). Biological sex was successfully estimated for all but one of the individuals. The results not only provide a more efficient biological sex estimation but also help to resolve a few errors in sex assessment previously encountered with osteomorphological and tooth morphometric techniques. The implementation of this method significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of biological sex estimation, offering a powerful tool for anthropological research.

abstract:
Objectives

When in energetically demanding environments (e.g., high altitude, backcountry expeditions), humans acclimatize to compounded intensive stressors. Acclimatization is possible in part by using the dynamically responsive neuroendocrine system, with changes to hormones like cortisol (CORT) and testosterone (T), which both play important metabolic roles. We sought to examine how these hormones change during acclimatization and what their relationship was to energetic outcomes (i.e., physical activity intensity and average energy expenditure (AEE)).

Materials and methods

Data were collected from 70 healthy individuals (age range: 18-53 years; female = 39) throughout a 3-month long expedition in the American Rockies. Repeated measures of pre-activity salivary baseline and acute change (i.e., reactivity) samples of CORT and T were taken throughout the 3-month period. Physical activity intensity and energy expenditure were also assessed in a subset of participants using the wGT3X-BT Actigraph monitor.

Results

Over the 3-month period, we found that time on the course moderated the relationship between CORT reactivity and physical activity intensity (%MVPA) and AEE. Compared to the start of the expedition, female baseline T was significantly higher in the middle and end, and male baseline T was significantly higher at the end. Additionally, female T acutely declined significantly more at the end of the expedition compared to the beginning. We also found that time on course and sex moderated the relationship between T reactivity and activity intensity.

Conclusions

These findings suggest a dynamic relationship between neuroendocrine and energetic outcomes during acclimatization, which may further differ between sexes.

abstract:
Objective

This study aimed to investigate the relationship between pelvic and lower extremity measurements obtained from orthoroentgenography images and stature, and to develop sex-specific stature estimation models based on these measurements.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study included 114 adult individuals (67 females and 47 males) with recorded stature. Sex-related differences were evaluated using the independent samples t-test. Associations between measurements were assessed separately for females and males using Pearson correlation analysis. Multiple linear regression, LASSO regression and Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines (MARS) models were constructed for stature estimation. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS (version 31.0) and R software (version 4.3.0), with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

Results

Most pelvic and lower extremity measurements showed statistically significant sex-based differences. Femur length emerged as a consistent and important predictor of stature in both sexes. In multiple linear regression analysis, the model including FL, SIJD, LTD, and CVH yielded an R2 value of 0.723 in males, whereas the model including FL and SIJD produced an R2 value of 0.40 in females. The MARS model yielded R2 values of 0.729 in males based on FL, SIJD, LTD, and CVH, and 0.420 in females based on FL and ICL.

Conclusion

Stature estimation based on pelvic and lower extremity measurements shows clear sex-specific differences. Both multiple linear regression and MARS models demonstrated higher explanatory performance in males than in females. These findings highlight the importance of sex-specific and multivariate modeling strategies and suggest that the proposed models may serve as complementary tools in forensic anthropology and clinical applications.

abstract: Reduction in brain weight is a hallmark feature of human aging, which is exacerbated in pathologies, such as Alzheimer's disease and other dementias. However, it remains unclear whether a decrease in brain weight with age reflects a vulnerability unique to the human lineage or represents a consequence of an extension of aging processes shared with other primates. To address this question, we examined age-related changes in brain weight across our closest living relatives, the great apes (chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas, and orangutans). The sample spanned the full adult age range in each species and included individuals reaching ages comparable to those at which age-related brain changes become apparent in humans. Across species, brain weight did not show significant change throughout adulthood and into advanced age. The observed pattern held even when body weight was included in the analysis in a subsample of chimpanzees. Overall, these results indicate that marked brain weight loss is not a general feature of great ape aging and instead appears largely specific to humans, with implications for understanding susceptibility to late-life brain pathology.

abstract: The target article by Stibbard Hawkes and von Rueden (SHVR) provides useful terminological housekeeping, but its individualistic account of egalitarianism in small-scale societies risks overlooking important group-level functions. We argue that egalitarian norms are not merely by-products of individual strategies but actively sustain cooperation, coordination, and collective decision-making, enhancing group stability and collective intelligence. A full account of egalitarianism must integrate both individual-level processes and emergent group-level outcomes. Egalitarianism not only constrains inequality but also underwrites the cooperative capacities of small-scale societies.

abstract:
Objective

To validate a Bayesian method for sex estimation from permanent canines (Luna, 2019) on an independent contemporary skeletal sample from Argentina.

Design

The study analyzed 152 permanent canines (61 upper, 91 lower) from 98 individuals (55 males, 43 females) included in the Prof. Dr. Rómulo Lambre Reference Collection (La Plata, Argentina). Buccolingual and mesiodistal diameters of the crown and neck region were measured. Bayesian posterior probabilities were computed for single- and multi-variable models, and classification accuracy was assessed against documented biological sex.

Results

The buccolingual neck diameter was the best single predictor, yielding accuracy rates of 73.77% (lower canines, p = 0.74) and 73.62% (lower canines, p = 0.74). Multi-variable models improved performance: using only the neck diameter, lower canines achieved 81.96% accuracy (p = 0.78), and upper canines, 80.21% (p = 0.80). The four-variable model produced the highest overall accuracy (lower: 85.24%, p = 0.85; upper: 83.51%, p = 0.83). Sex-specific correct classification rates ranged 80.77-83.33% for females and 83.63-88.57% for males, with posterior probabilities of 0.78-0.88 and 0.80-0.86, respectively.

Conclusions

Neck metrics demonstrate strong performance for sex estimation, proving particularly valuable for commingled or isolated remains. This Bayesian probabilistic framework provides transparent uncertainty estimates essential for forensic standards and can be successfully applied to contemporary non-identified individuals of similar geographical provenance.

abstract: The North American Free Trade Agreement, now the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, has increased semi-truck and vehicular traffic at international ports-of-entry, raising air pollution concerns in the US-Mexico border region. Studying the border county of El Paso, Texas, a central hub for Mexican imports, we extend the literature by examining the prevalence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) across census tracts with varying proximities to the port-of-entry, PM<sub>2.5</sub> exposure, and percent immigrant. We accomplish this objective by merging NASA PM<sub>2.5</sub> measurements with health data from the US Centers for Disease Control and social vulnerability indicators from the US Census' American Community Survey. We also use ArcGIS Pro to determine each census tract's proximity to a port-of-entry. Using Generalized Linear Models, we found that PM<sub>2.5</sub> and the percent foreign-born noncitizens are positively associated with COPD prevalence. Census tracts close to a port-of-entry, compared with those more than three miles away, have higher COPD prevalence. Moreover, COPD prevalence in immigrant communities and the effects of PM<sub>2.5</sub> are stratified across census tracts by proximity to ports-of-entry.

abstract: Chlordecone, a highly persistent organochlorine insecticide, was widely applied to banana plantations in Martinique and Guadeloupe from 1972 until being banned in 1993. Decades later, its residues still permeate soil, waterways, food systems, and human bodies in the two islands. Classified as both a carcinogenic and an endocrine disruptor, the chemical compound has generated widespread protests, epidemiological debates, and political critique. Drawing on six months of non-consecutive ethnographic fieldwork conducted in Martinique between 2017 and 2022, this article examines how people interpret and navigate the chemical's enduring effects. We develop the concept of 'articulations of poisoning' to describe the ways in which Chlordecone is rendered meaningful, not simply as a biomedical or ecological risk, but as a lived, historically sedimented, and politically contested experience. These articulations unfold along three interconnected dimensions (i.e. historicity, relationality, and contextuality) that shape how poisoning is perceived, embodied, and contested in everyday life. Through the voices of activists, farmers, medical professionals, institutional actors, and community members, we explore how poisoning becomes entangled with colonial legacies, political debates, and the everyday struggle for environmental justice in the French Antilles.

abstract: What is the place of health practitioners at sea? What role does this officer occupy, straddling the fields of dietetics, prevention and minor traumatology? Four printed books (little used in the history of medicine and medical anthropology) will serve as guides: Letters from a surgeon to Mr. … shipowner on the subject of the plant-based diet proposed for seafarers (M. Poissonnier des Perrières, 1773), Advice to seafarers on their health (G. Mauran, 1786), Lessons on asphyxia or instructions on the assistance to be given to drowned persons and others asphyxiated (L.S.C. Sauvé, 1841) and Treatise on naval hygiene (J.B. Fonssagrives, 1878). From the comparative analysis of these four works covering two centuries of health activity at sea, we will see what evolutionary paths were taken by these embarked practitioners. Far from the image of a simple "luxury barber", surgeons, pharmacists and other health practitioners acquired over time a function of hygienist, intervening in the very organization of life on board and during stopovers (meals, body care, prevention, etc.). They gradually became interested in the relationship between man and the environment, in professional risks and in work accidents (which he prevented and treated), etc. It was a new discipline that was being established, but also a new way of thinking and doing surgery/medicine and maintaining health.

abstract: Among the most damaging anticipated consequences of climate change are rising global temperatures that are expected to exceed the heat tolerance of many species worldwide. Species' heat tolerance reflects adaptation to their historical environments, and rapid increases in ambient temperatures create a mismatch between evolved thermal tolerance and present-day heat exposures. This mismatch has severe implications because high temperatures can disrupt physiological processes across levels of biological organization. The immune system, specifically, may be particularly susceptible to dysregulation under climate warming because it is highly responsive to temperature. Although a rich body of empirical and clinical research has characterized the effects of heat on immunity, these findings are rarely interpreted in the context of evolved heat tolerance. Here, we provide a framework for predicting the immunological consequences of climate change by integrating results derived from five decades of immune research with evolutionary principles of heat tolerance. This framework offers a strong foundation for predicting the health and disease consequences of immune vulnerability to heat in a rapidly warming world.

abstract: The Likouala-aux-Herbes river and surrounding swamp forests of the northern Republic of Congo are described in scientific literature as a wetland forest system characterized by a bimodal flood pulse and widespread seasonal flooding. Recent climatic and hydrological modelling of the Congo Basin and Cuvette Centrale peatlands, moreover, positions the Likouala region as a rain-fed or ombrotrophic peatland. However, human populations experience and adapt to flooding at a more localized scale. This study presents ethnographic data on flooding and seasonality from six villages within the Lac Télé Community Reserve (LTCR), a protected area in the Likouala swamp forest biome and the country's only Community Reserve. Our findings reveal how spatio-temporally variable flooding produces village-specific cultures, livelihood cycles, adaptations and vulnerabilities-an interconnected gradient of biocultural relationships. Across villages, flood dynamics have changed drastically over the last decades. Climate change, economic transitions and erosion of local knowledge systems are straining long-standing adaptive frameworks within and between LTCR communities. We emphasize the importance of ethnographic data in understanding fine-scale human-environment interactions and suggest that biocultural analysis at this scale-what we term the 'hydrocultural patch'-is essential for effective landscape governance and policy development in the context of accelerating climate change. A French translation of this abstract is available in the supplementary material.         This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'African tropical peatlands: function, value and vulnerability'.

abstract: Statistical calibration of the results in adult age-at-death estimation is a fundamental yet challenging task in forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology. This study conducts a large-scale Bayesian validation of two probabilistic models for adult dental age-at-death estimation: the established FIDBv2, using root dentin translucency and periodontal retraction, and a novel simplified counterpart, FIDBv3, relying solely on translucency. Analysis of 8,595 single-rooted teeth from a global sample of 3,801 individuals demonstrates that FIDBv3 consistently outperforms its predecessor, reducing overall mean inaccuracy by 22.52% and increasing total sample accuracy by 8.11 percentage points. This superior performance across diverse populations indicates that periodontal retraction introduces more statistical noise than a reliable biological signal. The strategic exclusion of this variable, combined with the inclusion of a logarithmic transformation that better models the non-linear trajectory of translucency development, yields a more biologically realistic and universally applicable method. This simplification also streamlines analysis, while deployment as a free, open-access web platform democratizes global access to this robust, probability-based estimation. Despite persistent challenges at the extremes of the lifespan, FIDBv3 establishes a new standard for transparent, reliable and practical dental age-at-death estimation in forensic and archaeological contexts.

abstract: "Trauma" has become a widely circulating cultural framework for making suffering intelligible. Sociological research has documented its institutional expansion but paid less attention to how people use it to organize experiences that disrupt orientation to body, self, and world. This article examines that situated process in non-clinical psychedelic contexts. Drawing on 48 in-depth interviews with people who defined their psychedelic experiences as challenging, we trace how participants mobilized trauma discourse in response to ontological rupture. The analysis identifies five configurations of therapeutic sense-making: somatic discovery of trauma, embodied re-experiencing, the experience as healing instruction, the recursive healing project, and the limits of therapeutic sense-making. Across the first four, trauma discourse condensed diverse suffering into an authoritative category and supplied vocabularies for sequencing experience and directing action; we use personalization to describe how this shared framework becomes biographically meaningful. The fifth captures the cases where personalization broke down: the framework felt imposed, became a performance for others, or disclosed memories and revelations participants could not hold as real. Our abductive analysis of these cases generated three dimensions of authenticity: subjective ownership, non-performance, and realness. The findings point to a structural tension: we suggest that circulating trauma discourse beyond credentialed clinical and ritual authorities both expands the framework's flexibility and leaves personalization vulnerable to social pressure, unaccountable authority, and unresolved epistemic uncertainty. This study extends sociological critiques of therapeutization by shifting attention from the diffusion of therapeutic frameworks to the conditions of their uptake.

abstract: In this paper, we discuss the practical and moral complexities of diagnostic-seeking pathways for three uncertain medical conditions: fibromyalgia, myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), and long COVID. We analyse qualitative data collected in the UK between 2023 and 2025, comprising in-depth interviews with medical professionals, researchers, and patients, as well as documentary sources. Drawing on the anthropology and sociology of diagnosis, this paper discusses how chronic illness can be marked by challenging and unstable pathways, influenced by the organisation of the medical system and the resources patients have to navigate it. Diagnoses further do not guarantee a solution to the condition, and can, on the other hand, produce stigma. Medical professionals recognise the uncertain nature of these conditions and emphasise how diagnosis can play an instrumental role in providing patients with access to therapies, benefits, or acceptance. Patients discuss the complexity of the strategies they deploy not only to obtain a diagnosis but also to navigate the practical and moral complexities associated with their condition. Analysing the practical and moral complexity of diagnostic-seeking pathways represents a way to enrich anthropological reflections on diagnosis by demonstrating how this key concept of biomedicine is strongly influenced by social, economic, and moral, as well as biological, factors.

abstract: In some Sino-Tibetan languages, the gustatory term meaning 'sour' is widely used to describe somatosensory states such as muscle aches, exertional soreness, and tender sensations during acupuncture: a sensation called sngception. This study draws from the fields of linguistic anthropology, medical humanities, and corpus linguistics to investigate the cultural-historical and cognitive basis of sngception. Through a corpus analysis of modern Mandarin Chinese, the current study examined the semantic patterns and collocations of suān () 'sour.' With current medical findings on acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs), the sourness metaphor emerges as both physiologically and culturally grounded. Such cultural-linguistic frameworks play a significant role in shaping how discomfort is perceived and interpreted, which calls for greater attention to clinical awareness of culturally embedded expressions of pain in intercultural healthcare settings.

abstract: The chemosteometric regression models proposed by Gonçalves et al. (2020) based on data obtained through Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy in attenuated total reflectance mode provided encouraging results regarding the prediction of heat-induced metric changes in human bone. In this study, the potential of chemosteometry was further explored by adding powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) data. Bones from six experimentally burnt human skeletons from the 21st Century Identified Skeletal Collection (four females and two males with ages at death between 62 and 88 years) were measured before and after burning. Cortical bone was sampled from each bone and analysed through FTIR-ATR and XRD. The resulting data were used to build regression models to predict the percentage of heat-induced metric changes. Results were then compared to the actual metric changes. Chemometric data that most significantly correlated with such changes were the infrared band at 3572 cm<sup>-1</sup>(hydroxyapatite OH stretch) and the XRD crystallite size. The infrared crystallinity index also provided relevant information for the regression models. Adjusted R<sup>2</sup> of the regression models ranged between 0.20 and 0.68 and mean absolute error (MAE) values ranged between 2.59 and 4.22 percentage points. Models based only on the maximum length of clavicles, metacarpals and metatarsals provided even better predictions, suggesting that results vary according to bone type. In contrast, correction factors of 10%, 12% and 15% resulted in higher MAE of 5.50, 6.34 and 8.20 percentage points in the same sample, respectively. The added benefit of adding the XRD crystallite size to models including FTIR data was ambiguous, appearing to be irrelevant for the overall sample, but improving estimations in the subsample that only comprised bones with diaphysis. The results suggest that the prediction of heat-induced shrinkage in epiphyseal measurements is to some extent undermined by using FTIR and XRD data obtained from cortical bone samples. This study concluded that chemosteometry provides an objective case-by-case prediction of heat-induced shrinkage, having clear advantages over the shrinkage correction factor approach.

abstract: With the advent of advanced computational methods, facial identification has evolved from traditional anthropometric techniques to machine-learning and deep-learning models capable of recognizing the distinctive morphological features of the face. The human face is one of the most distinctive features of an individual's identity, providing investigators with a non-invasive means of narrowing down the suspects and identifying the victims. The present study explores the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for the classification and identification of Himalayan populations using facial features. Human faces from the upper and lower Himalayan regions of Himachal Pradesh State in the northern India were studied. A novel AI model has been developed to enhance facial recognition capabilities. The developed AI model particularly focuses on classifying individuals from the upper and lower Himalayan regions based on their facial features. Morphologically, the upper Himalayan population groups can be distinguished from the lower Himalayan population groups in their overall facial shapes, shape and size of the nose and eyes, and so on. The phenotypic differences observed in a population may vary due to both intra-observer and inter-observer assessments. The CNN models have the potential to extract peculiar facial features with a high level of accuracy. In the present study, the designed model yielded a training accuracy of 89.32% and the validation accuracy of 86.00%. Moreover, the highest validation accuracy of 88.02% was achieved at epoch 109, indicating its reliability and effectiveness in facial classification. In addition, the individual and average Grad-CAM analysis was performed to visually confirm that which region is contributing more to the CNN classification. The customized AI model shows its potential applications for individual identification, ethnicity classification, facial identification research work, security and surveillance, forensic examinations, border control, and crime scene investigations.

abstract:
Background

Mortality and disability after injuries are high in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs). Improving outcomes for injured patients requires knowledge of their associated factors. We aimed to assess post-injury mortality and disability and their associations with access to health care across LMICs with different injury burdens, health-care systems, and contexts.

Methods

Hospitalised patients in Ghana, Pakistan, Rwanda, and South Africa with moderate-to-severe injuries were recruited and followed up until 3 months after discharge or death. Injured patients of any age who were admitted to facilities for more than 12 h or died within 12 h of admission were included. Data were collected between Feb 17, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, using the REDCap electronic data platform. Our primary outcome was a composite of 3-month mortality or moderate-to-severe disability (assessed using the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule). Secondary outcomes were disability at 3 months after discharge, mortality up to 3 months after discharge (including in-hospital mortality), and in-hospital mortality. In multivariable analysis, we tested the associations of these outcomes with access to health-care variables of previous health-care encounters, transport to the hospital (private vs ambulance vs other), delays in reaching the hospital, and hospital level (secondary vs tertiary), controlling for age, sex, education, wealth, and injury type and severity.

Findings

9720 patients admitted to 19 hospitals capable of providing definitive care for injuries, serving urban and rural settings, were eligible for inclusion in the study. Of those, 8858 (91·1%; 6788 male, 2047 female, and 23 [<1%] with missing sex data; median age 31 years [IQR 20-43]) were enrolled and 8687 (89·4%) completed hospital follow-up, with 5835 patients followed up at 3 months. At 3 months, 2476 (47·6%) of 5199 patients with available primary outcome data had died or were disabled. In-hospital mortality was 6·1% (531 of 8687), 3-month mortality was 9·7% (616 of 6366), and 3-month disability was 40·6% (1860 of 4583). Higher odds of the primary outcome were associated with arrival by ambulance (odds ratio 1·86, 95% CI 1·51-2·29), and lower odds were associated with a previous health-care encounter (0·61, 0·52-0·71). Hospital level (1·14, 0·96-1·35) and delays in reaching the facility (0·86, 0·74-1·00) were not associated with the primary outcome.

Interpretation

The high post-injury mortality and disability are associated with health system factors that must be better understood before potentially expensive service models are introduced or expanded. Investment in pre-hospital care, ambulance systems, and centralised specialist trauma centres is unlikely to achieve its intended benefits unless services are appropriately planned, integrated, coordinated, and staffed across the care pathway. High-quality routine data are also essential to guide service improvement and enable robust quasi-experimental evaluations of whether these investments improve patient outcomes, for whom, and under what circumstances.

abstract: The medical education in the BRICs countries plays key role in ensuring technological sovereignty of member countries. The article explores innovative approaches to medical education in the BRICs countries. The special attention is paid to project training as a tool to form professional competencies of future specialists. The analysis was applied to such successful practices of the BRICs countries as development of telemedicine, international cooperation and organization of joint research projects. The main challenges, including personnel deficiency and inequality member countries in fitting-out education sphere are highlighted. The article emphasizes role of medical education in ensuring technological sovereignty and proposes directions for further cooperation between the BRICs member countries. The key element of work of physician today are technologies related to long-term monitoring of patient permitting to survive the longest life. On the example of project and research activities of leading Russian and foreign universities, the model of integration of science, education and practical health care is developed to ensure training of highly qualified medical personnel. The key trends in digital transformation of education are considered, including application of AI, cloud technologies and personalized approach to solution of clinical problems in education process.

abstract:
Background

Clinical teaching occurs where patient care and education coexist. Within the United Kingdom's National Health Service, workforce pressures constrain teaching and supervision. Clinical Teaching Fellow (CTF) roles have expanded in response but are often viewed as discrete posts rather than practices situated within complex clinical-educational systems. This study examined how tensions within and across these systems shaped CTF practice.

Methods

This theory-informed exploratory qualitative case study used third-generation Activity Theory. All 10 members of a hospital medical education team were invited to a semistructured group interview; eight participated. An Activity Theory-informed thematic approach was used to map the focal undergraduate clinical education activity system and examine tensions within it and at its intersections with adjacent systems.

Findings

Participants included three CTFs, two education facilitators and three administrators. CTF practice involved teaching, programme coordination and administrative work within a multiprofessional team. Differing understandings of the activity's purpose and outcomes shaped practice. Professional language, continuity, experience and blurred divisions of labour influenced participation and work organisation. Relationships with clinical services, the medical school, postgraduate medical education and university-based postgraduate study introduced competing demands. Participants negotiated tensions through communication, redistribution of responsibilities and closer working across professional roles.

Conclusions

CTF roles are embedded within systems where educational, clinical and organisational priorities intersect. Third-generation Activity Theory makes visible how relationships within and across these systems shape practice. Supporting CTF roles requires attention to how educational work is organised, coordinated and prioritised.

abstract: The article considers digital tutorship as modern mechanism for development of professional competencies of medical professionals in the context of digital transformation of health care and transition to model of continuing medical education. abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI (GenAI), is reshaping clinical care and medical education, requiring medical education faculty to develop new competencies. As GenAI becomes integrated into clinical and teaching workflows, faculty must guide learners in AI-enabled environments. Although existing frameworks outline AI competencies for clinicians or learners, few synthesise competencies specifically for faculty roles. This review addresses that gap by synthesising AI and GenAI competency frameworks to identify GenAI domains relevant to medical education faculty.

Methods

The authors conducted a narrative review of 24 articles published between January 2020 and February 2025 on AI and GenAI competencies for clinicians, educators and learners. Structured database searches identified articles. Existing AI competency frameworks guided comparison of faculty-relevant GenAI competencies. Through iterative synthesis, the authors identified competency domains consistently represented across frameworks and aligned with educator responsibilities.

Findings

Using Russell et al.'s framework as an organising anchor, six competency domains were identified: (1) Foundational AI Knowledge and Literacy; (2) Ethical, Social, and Legal Policies and Implications; (3) AI-Enhanced Clinical Interactions; (4) Practice-Based Learning, Instructional Design, and Pedagogy; (5) Evidence-Based Evaluation and Assessment; and (6) Systems-Level Workflow and Integration. Existing frameworks differed in emphasis across domains, with clinical and systems-level competencies less consistently represented.

Implications

These domains provide a foundational structure to guide faculty development, curricular decision-making and responsible integration of GenAI into medical education. Future work should translate these domains into observable indicators and assessment strategies while examining how faculty competencies support learner development and responsible GenAI use.

abstract: Self-control denotes the capacity to intentionally pursue actions that align with long-term, meaningful goals. Although cumulative evidence has shown that parental-adolescent attachment and peer attachment are closely associated with self-control, the longitudinal links between mother attachment, father attachment, peer attachment, and self-control are unclear. This study utilized Random-Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Models (RI-CLPMs) to analyse longitudinal data from 1312 Chinese adolescents (age range 12-18, Mage = 14.29, SD = 1.38; 50.2% boys) over 1 year with three measurements (i.e., 6 months apart across three cohorts). After separating within-person and between-person associations, the results from the RI-CLPMs revealed that, at the between-person level, both parental-adolescent attachment (including attachment to both mother and father) and peer attachment were positively associated with self-control. At the within-person level, cross-lagged effects were found between mother attachment and self-control. Additionally, self-control was found to positively predict subsequent father attachment and peer attachment. Furthermore, father attachment at T2 positively predicted self-control at T3, while peer attachment at T1 positively predicted self-control at T2. The differing findings regarding mother attachment, father attachment, and peer attachment highlight the importance of considering various significant figures in the study of attachment and self-control.

abstract: Both positive and negative family interactions are closely associated with adolescent mental health. Using an integrated point of view, this study used a longitudinal design to examine the interplay patterns of family support and family incivility on adolescent mental health. Two waves of data were collected from 999 Chinese high school students. Polynomial regressions and response surface analyses were used to examine interplay patterns of family support and incivility, specifically, their congruence effect and incongruence effect on mental health outcomes, including well-being (life satisfaction and meaning in life) and psychopathological symptoms (anxiety and depressive symptoms). Model comparison was conducted within a series of models to select the best fitting model for each mental health outcome. As for positive mental health outcomes, both life satisfaction and meaning in life had a curvilinear correlation with the incongruence of family support and family incivility. The correlations were larger when family support was higher than family incivility than vice versa. Additionally, a significant interaction effect of family support and family incivility was found on meaning in life. Specifically, the positive association between family support and meaning in life was weaker when family incivility was high. As for negative mental health outcomes, both anxiety and depressive symptoms were linearly correlated with the incongruence of family support and family incivility. Specifically, greater family support relative to family incivility was associated with lower levels of anxiety and depressive symptoms. These findings promoted understanding of the impact of family environment on adolescent mental health and highlighted the importance of considering both positive and negative forms of family interaction.

abstract: Spiritual education in the People's Republic of China has grown out of concerns for students' holistic development, socialist ideology education, patriotic education, moral cultivation, and traditional Chinese philosophy. Spiritual education is considered as inner development, emotional awareness, moral character and the quest for meaning in Chinese scholars; however, in practice, it tends to appear more and more in the ideological context of the Party-state. The focus of this article is the incorporation and transformation of spiritual education in the state ideology of the People's Republic of China, and how spiritual education has been conceptually translated into moral education, ideological and political education, patriotic education, socialist core values and cultural-confidence discourse. Based on qualitative documentary analysis and an integrative literature review, the study draws on academic works, laws on education, policy documents, teaching practice and research on spiritual education, moral education, Confucian revival, nationalism and ideological-political education in China and uses the descriptive national education statistics from 2024 to provide context to the institutional scale of the education system. Based on the findings, spiritual education has not yet become a field of religious or theological education as a whole in the PRC. Instead, its language and purposes have been turned into state-friendly education goals like moral values, social responsibility, patriotism, national unity, cultural confidence, and dedication to national renewal. Traditional values and norms, particularly those related to self-cultivation, harmony, filial duty and the affection of family country, have been picked up and incorporated into the process with a specific purpose of strengthening socialist citizenship and ideological cohesion. In modern China spiritual education may be understood as an area of moral-political education. It still includes an interest in inner growth, emotional development, moral character and social responsibility, but has been increasingly influenced by the ideology of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the leadership of the Chinese Communist Party in its institutional form. This situation provides opportunities for holistic education, yet also brings up issues about pluralism, critical thinking, students' autonomy, and moral education and political socialization.

abstract: The molecular characterization of genetically modified plants is commonly based on the detection of foreign DNA sequences introduced during transformation. While this strategy is effective for conventional transgenic plants, it becomes inadequate for cisgenic and intragenic plants in which the introduced gene originates from the host genome and is regulated by native promoter and terminator elements. Following segregation-based elimination of selectable marker cassettes, such cisgenic plants may become indistinguishable from wild-type plants using standard sequence-dependent PCR assays. This chapter presents a quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) and computation-based approach for estimating gene copy number as an auxiliary molecular marker for the analysis of cisgenic plant lines. The method relies on quantitative differences in endogenous gene dosage rather than the detection of heterologous DNA. Genomic DNA from putative cisgenic and control plants is analyzed by qPCR using serial template dilutions and primer pairs targeting both a cisgenic candidate gene and an endogenous single-copy reference gene. Linear regression of cycle threshold (Ct) values against log₂-transformed DNA concentrations is performed, and differences in regression intercepts are used to infer relative gene copy number. Because the underlying data processing, regression modeling, and copy number calculations may be technically demanding for routine users, a dedicated standalone computational tool, CisScope, was developed to automate the entire analytical workflow. CisScope integrates data parsing, statistical modeling, and result interpretation into an intuitive graphical interface and is distributed as an executable file, eliminating the need for programming expertise or specialized statistical software. Although not intended for regulatory diagnostics, this integrated experimental, computational framework offers a practical and accessible solution to a major limitation of sequence-based detection strategies in cisgenic plant biotechnology and is well-suited for both research and educational applications.

abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) is disrupting healthcare and health professions education (HPE), creating complex ethical challenges. Despite existing governance frameworks, postgraduate and continuing professional development (CPD) learners require stronger micro-level ethical competence. However, AI-ethics remains insufficiently integrated into postgraduate/CPD curricula with few real-world reflective and interprofessional strategies, raising concerns regarding ethical preparedness. The aim of this study is to map how AI ethics is taught within postgraduate/CPD HPE, drawing on principlism, an ethical framework espousing the principles of autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence and justice and transformative learning theory (TLT), which explains how critical reflection transforms professional assumptions, perspectives and practice.

Method

A systematic search of six databases (2000-2025) was conducted to identify relevant sources. Data extraction captured study design, educational setting, pedagogical strategies and ethical themes. Findings were synthesised descriptively and narratively to examine empirical rigour, theoretical alignment and relevance to contemporary generative-AI developments.

Results

Sixteen eligible sources were identified. Only 31% were empirical studies. The evidence reflected a strong Western worldview. AI-ethics education for postgraduate/CPD learners was limited, often superficial and reliant on varied but weakly evaluated pedagogies. Principlism appeared frequently but mostly implicitly, whereas explicit application of TLT was rare. Major gaps included low empirical and pedagogical rigour, minimal interprofessionalism and marked temporal anachronism, as most studies predated the advent of generative AI.

Conclusion

AI-ethics education in postgraduate/CPD HPE remains conceptually rich but pedagogically underdeveloped. Effective curricula require structured, theory-anchored, interprofessional and culturally responsive approaches. Integrating principlism and TLT as ethical and pedagogical frameworks may strengthen ethical competence and preparedness.

abstract: Menstrual cycle tracking is a much-discussed component of the ' female athlete' research theme; however, more translational work is needed to meet practitioners' desire for further guidance on the implementation of tracking in applied settings. The purpose of this paper is to present a preliminary conceptual model to inform practitioners' decision-making around menstrual cycle tracking and assist researchers in identifying and framing future research directions. The proposed model-Conducting and Navigating menstrual cycle Education, Communication and Tracking (ConNECT)-proposes that communication and education strategies may be utilised to affect social, organisational and individual level change, ultimately supporting the implementation of menstrual cycle tracking by increasing its uptake and impact. This model was developed based on the findings from a series of studies conducted by the authors, which considered the existing literature on tracking and the perspectives of athletes and practitioners. Therefore, the ConNECT model offers an ecologically sound starting point for sport scientists, coaches and other members of an athlete's support team to base their practice on.

abstract:
Background

Total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplantation (TPIAT) requires families to manage diabetes with insulin pumps and continuous glucose monitors postoperatively at our institution. Education occurs while the child is hospitalized after TPIAT, and one parent or caregiver receives all education. Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) must be effective, efficient, and completed with enough time for families to practice before discharge. We created a pre-TPIAT diabetes education program aimed at reducing subsequent inpatient education time and increasing the primary learner's preparedness for inpatient education.

Methods

Thirty-three pediatric TPIAT recipients at Cincinnati Children's received presurgery education across three cycles of improvement. Data were extracted from clinical records and survey responses collected. Cohorts were well-balanced demographically (all P > 0.05, small effect sizes). Survey data, including paired knowledge assessments, were collected from Cohorts 2 and 3.

Results

TPIAT recipients were predominantly White (87.9%), English speaking, non-Hispanic (97.0%), with balanced sex distribution (48.5% female). Mean age at surgery was 12.2 years. Parents were primary learners in 87.9% of cases. Presurgery education time showed highly statistically significant increases in Cohorts 2 and 3 compared with Cohort 1 (P = 0.0291 and P = 0.0007, respectively). Inpatient diabetes education showed a marginally significant decrease of 133 min from Cohort 1 to Cohort 2 (P = 0.0717) and directionally maintained in Cohort 3 (0.3285). Assessment results documented substantial knowledge acquisition from the intervention that was retained from pre- to postsurgery education. Learner confidence increased postintervention (P = 0.063), and overall satisfaction scores remained high except for stress/anxiety scores.

Conclusion

Changes in TPIAT diabetes education delivery effectively transferred some education to presurgery without compromising content, demonstrated by a statistically significant increase in presurgery education, knowledge scores that indicated retention of information, alongside numerically lower (nonsignificant) total inpatient education time after interventions.

abstract: Accurate determination of cysteine (Cys) remains challenging because of the structural similarity and comparable nucleophilicity of biological thiols. Herein, a red-emissive turn-on fluorescent probe, TCF-C1, was developed for selective Cys detection by coupling an acrylate recognition unit with a thiophene-extended TCF fluorophore. Reaction with Cys triggered a conjugate addition-cyclization process, resulting in the release of highly fluorescent TCF-OH and a pronounced fluorescence enhancement at 664 nm, accompanied by a visible color change from pink to purple. TCF-C1 exhibited a rapid response within 10 min and high selectivity for Cys over homocysteine, glutathione, amino acids, and common inorganic ions, together with a large Stokes shift of approximately 160 nm. The fluorescence intensity showed a linear dependence on Cys concentration from 0 to 35 µM, with a detection limit of 32.91 nM. The proposed sensing mechanism was supported by ESI-MS analysis and theoretical calculations. In addition, TCF-C1 exhibited low cytotoxicity and enabled fluorescence imaging of endogenous and exogenous Cys in living cells. Its analytical applicability was further demonstrated by the determination of Cys in samples of spinach, broccoli, snap beans, and carrots. These results establish TCF-C1 as a simple and sensitive fluorescent probe for Cys determination in food samples and for cellular imaging.

abstract: The derivative is a fundamental concept in engineering education, as it enables students to model and interpret phenomena related to rates of change, optimization, and the analysis of physical processes. However, its teaching in higher education often emphasizes decontextualized algebraic procedures, with limited integration of authentic engineering problems and interactive digital technologies. This protocol outlines a scoping review aimed at mapping the available evidence on teaching and learning strategies for the derivative in undergraduate engineering education that incorporate authentic engineering problems, with or without the support of digital technologies. The review will follow the methodological framework proposed by the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis and the reporting guidelines of PRISMA-ScR. The review is guided by the PCC framework: (P) undergraduate engineering students; (C) didactic strategies for teaching and learning the derivative grounded in authentic engineering problems, with or without the support of digital technologies; and (C) higher education engineering programs. Searches will be conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and SciELO for peer-reviewed publications published between 2000 and 2026 in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Two reviewers will independently screen and select studies using Rayyan, and disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Data will be extracted using a pilot-tested data extraction form and synthesized through descriptive statistics, thematic categorization, and narrative synthesis. The review will provide a comprehensive mapping of didactic strategies, types of authentic problems, and reported learning difficulties related to the derivative in engineering education. The findings are expected to inform instructional design and support the development of evidence-based teaching practices in calculus courses for engineering students.

abstract: Individuals from regions affected by infectious disease outbreaks may be stigmatized because others hold negative mental images-or mental representations-of them. This study investigated whether such outbreaks lead to the formation of negative mental representations of residents in affected areas and explored the role of disease severity in this process. Study 1 revealed that during the early stages of the COVID-19 epidemic, the public's mental representations of residents from Wuhan were perceived as less attractive than those of Chengdu residents and associated with disgust and behavioural avoidance. However, differences disappeared after the restrictions of the epidemic were lifted. The results indicate that the COVID-19 outbreak triggered stigmatization of residents in Wuhan. In Study 2, disease severity and perceived threat were manipulated, and results show that participants formed less attractive face representations of residents from areas where severe infectious diseases broke out than those from areas affected by mild infectious diseases. This proved that the severity of infectious diseases affected the extent of stigmatization towards residents in outbreak areas. These results further our understanding of the mechanisms and factors underlying stigmatization associated with affected regions and may inform effective public health strategies to mitigate stigma and support disease control efforts.

abstract: Competency-based education (CBE) is gaining prominence in post-secondary education due to its effectiveness in optimizing workforce readiness. However, assessing competence and workforce readiness presents a significant challenge. Entrustable professional activities (EPAs) offer a promising solution by translating competencies into observable, entrustable tasks. While EPAs have been widely adopted in clinical training, their application in non-clinical educational contexts remains minimal. Guided by Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory, this scoping review aims to map the diffusion of EPAs beyond medical education and examine their scalability to non-clinical educational contexts, where real-world practice errors may undermine system integrity, educational outcomes, or public trust. This review will progress through five stages following Arksey and O'Malley's framework. Searches will be conducted across Ovid MEDLINE, CINAHL, Scopus, ERIC, and Google Scholar. The research question is: "How have EPAs been adapted, developed and implemented outside of medical education, and what factors influence their adoption in non-clinical educational contexts?" The search will include studies that describe, evaluate, or reflect on the adaptation, development, or implementation of EPAs outside medical education, and exclude studies that only propose, define, or discuss EPAs, focus on medical education, or are not published in English. Titles and abstracts will be reviewed first, followed by the full-text examination of relevant studies. Data will be extracted and summarized to highlight key findings. A two-reviewer protocol will ensure quality during screening and data extraction. The findings from this review may provide practical guidance for faculty, curriculum developers, institutional administration, industry partners, and accrediting or policy bodies involved in curriculum and assessment framework design. Further, the findings may inform the rationale for scaling EPA-based assessment frameworks to non-clinical educational contexts and offer recommendations to guide their adaptation, development, and implementation, addressing CBE assessment challenges and creating a replicable model for future non-clinical program development.
